Later meta-analytic work separated task cohesion from social cohesion; Anthony King's The Combat Soldier (2013) locates effectiveness in collective drill and professional practice rather than in affection; Omer Bartov's work on the Eastern Front argues ideology and coercion did work the primary-group model assigns elsewhere, and is itself disputed by primary-group theorists.
entries.application: Decide which version of cohesion the book is running on and let it be visible in how the unit trains, not only in how it feels. Band of brothers used as an explanation rather than a description is a 1948 finding wearing a 1990s phrase.

entries.name: What the Evidence Supports Is Task Cohesion, and Soldiers Did Not Mostly Name Solidarity
entries.description: The performance evidence favours shared commitment to the job over interpersonal liking — and when soldiers were actually asked, most named something else entirely.
entries.principle: Cohesion that predicts performance is cohesion about the task. Liking one another shows a weaker relationship and, on one analysis, no reliable effect once task cohesion is controlled for — a control the later replication could not reproduce.
entries.example: Mullen and Copper's meta-analysis reported task cohesion correlating with performance at around .43 and social cohesion around .27; Beal and colleagues reported .25 and .17 and could not replicate the control analysis. Separately, in Stouffer's wartime surveys about 14 per cent of soldiers cited solidarity with the group as what kept them going and about 39 per cent cited ending the task — a result usually omitted from the popularised account built on the same data. Transfer of the meta-analytic findings to combat specifically is disputed.
entries.application: Give the unit a job it is collectively committed to, and let the friendships be a by-product rather than the mechanism. Fiction that makes affection load-bearing has chosen the weaker of the two effects.

entries.name: Courage Is a Finite Account, Not a Trait
entries.description: Courage behaves like capital that is spent rather than like a quality a person has or lacks.
entries.principle: Endurance under fire draws down a reserve that is expended by exposure and only partly replenished by rest. A soldier who has been brave for months is not a brave man; he is a man with less left, and the pattern is observable long before it is visible.
entries.example: Lord Moran's The Anatomy of Courage (1945), written from his regimental medical service in the First World War and his observation in the Second, is the field's organising account — clinical observation rather than measurement, and treated as such.
entries.application: Track the account across the book and let it run down. The brave character and the cowardly character as fixed types are the version of this that the literature specifically contradicts.

entries.name: Everyone Has a Breaking Point, and the Famous Number Is Not Sourceable
entries.description: The principle that continuous combat exposure breaks nearly everyone is established; the widely quoted figure for how many days it takes is contested and could not be traced to a primary source.
entries.principle: Breakdown under sustained combat is a function of exposure rather than of character, and the wartime psychiatric literature treats it as near-universal given enough time. The variable is how long, not whether — but the specific threshold that circulates in the popular literature is not verified.
entries.example: The Second World War US Army psychiatric findings establish the principle. The frequently repeated claim that breakdown becomes near-universal after a specific span of continuous combat days is attributed to Swank and Marchand (1946), and the figure could not be confirmed against a primary source in this build's research; it is carried as a documentation gap rather than as a fact.
entries.application: Break the character on exposure rather than on temperament, and do not put the number in the book. The inexhaustible veteran is the failure this rule corrects; a precise threshold quoted as established is the failure it introduces.

entries.name: Forward Psychiatry Returns Men to Duty, and Most Break Again Quickly
entries.description: Treating psychiatric casualties near the front returns a majority to combat, and their recovery is measured in weeks. Period-bound to the US Army in the Second World War.
entries.principle: The doctrine of treating close to the front, immediately, and with the expectation of return produces high return-to-duty rates, and those rates conceal the durability of the result. Return to duty is not recovery; it is a delay whose length the data specify.
entries.example: The US Army's Second World War neuropsychiatry official history records that of those returned to combat duty, roughly 70 per cent were effective for only about six weeks before symptoms recurred, and men returned from base hospitals lasted about three weeks; recurrent cases made up about 12 per cent of admissions at advanced base hospitals, and average hospitalisation for acute cases ran around eleven days.
entries.application: If the book treats a psychiatric casualty, let the treatment work and then let it not hold. The recovery arc in which treatment restores the soldier is the shape this data specifically refuses.

entries.name: Panic Is a Process With a Shape
entries.description: Units do not break instantaneously; they break through an observable sequence that can be interrupted at several points.
entries.principle: Rout follows a recognisable order — rumour, an exposed or believed-exposed flank, the loss or absence of the leader, a drift rearward that nobody names as flight, and then flight. Each stage is a place where the process can be stopped, which is what officers and NCOs are for at that moment.
entries.example: The sequence is described consistently from Bull Run in 1861 to the French collapse in 1940, and Ardant du Picq's Battle Studies (published posthumously in 1880) records the fugitive moment directly, though his own evidence base is anecdotal.
entries.application: Write the drift before the flight. Panic as a switch removes both the officers' function and the several minutes in which the book's outcome is actually decided.

entries.name: Exemplary Punishment Is Aimed at Spectators, and Commutation Was the Normal Outcome
entries.description: Military capital punishment operated as deterrence directed at the living, and the great majority of death sentences were never carried out. Period-bound to the British and Commonwealth armies, 1914–18; the interpretation is contested.
entries.principle: The system's power lay in the possibility of execution rather than its frequency, and the sentence and the execution were separate events with very different probabilities. Armies understood the audience for the punishment to be the unit, not the condemned.
entries.example: Of roughly 3,080 death sentences passed in the British and Commonwealth armies in the First World War, 346 were carried out — about one in nine. Of the men executed, 91 were already under suspended sentence and 41 had had a previous death sentence commuted; 309 were pardoned by the United Kingdom in 2006 under the Armed Forces Act. The interpretation is genuinely disputed: campaigners read the executions as a category of injustice, while Cathryn Corns and John Hughes-Wilson in Blindfold and Alone (2001) argue for reading the cases individually and within their legal context. The pack records both readings and adjudicates neither. In the US Army, by contrast, Eddie Slovik's execution in January 1945 was the only one for desertion since the Civil War, against tens of thousands of desertion convictions.
entries.application: Separate the sentence from the execution in the narrative, and treat the routine outcome as commutation. Fiction in which armies shoot deserters as a matter of course has described a practice most armies mostly did not have.

entries.name: A Unit That Loses a Large Fraction of Its Strength Is Replaced, Not Rebuilt
entries.description: A shattered formation that returns to the line under the same number is a different organisation with different skills.
entries.principle: Skill, local knowledge and working relationships live in people, and when enough of them are gone the reconstituted unit retains only the designation. The paperwork records continuity; the capability does not.
entries.example: The reconstitution of shattered divisions on both sides in the Second World War is documented in the replacement and reconstitution histories, and the observed loss of unit identity and proficiency is consistent across them.
entries.application: Let the rebuilt unit be worse, and let the survivors notice. The depleted formation that recovers and is itself again erases the only permanent consequence most units suffer.

entries.name: Rotation Policy Determines What the War Feels Like to Fight
entries.description: Whether a soldier serves for a fixed tour or for the duration changes the psychology of the whole army. Period-bound; the two systems are not interchangeable.
entries.principle: A fixed individual tour gives every soldier a date and makes the approach of that date a behavioural variable; service for the duration removes the date and replaces it with wounding or the war's end as the only exits. These produce different units, different risk-taking and different veterans.
entries.example: US practice in the Second World War kept men in for the duration; Vietnam's twelve-month individual tour, thirteen for Marines, produced documented effects on unit cohesion and on short-timer behaviour as a soldier's date approached.
entries.application: Establish the tour structure early, because it silently governs what characters will risk. Transplanting one war's rotation system into another's is an error that changes every character's motivation without the writer noticing.

entries.name: Discipline and Cohesion Can Substitute for Each Other
entries.description: Effective units are not necessarily likeable ones; coercion, ideology and drill have all done the work that cohesion theory assigns to mutual regard. Contested.
entries.principle: An army can hold together through what its members owe each other or through what the institution will do to them, and formations have fought effectively on either basis. Treating social cohesion as necessary for effectiveness is an assumption the historical cases do not support.
entries.example: Omer Bartov's work on the German army on the Eastern Front argues that ideology and coercive discipline sustained units whose primary groups had been destroyed by casualties, and primary-group theorists dispute that reading directly; Anthony King's account locates effectiveness in professional drill rather than in either. The dispute is live and the pack does not settle it.
entries.application: Decide what actually holds the book's unit together and be willing for the answer to be unattractive. A pack of frightened men held in place by an institution is a truer and less comfortable unit than a family.

entries.name: Moral Injury Is Not the Same Wound as Fear
entries.description: The aftermath of combat includes an injury caused by betrayal of what is right, which behaves differently from fear-based trauma. Contested at its boundary.
entries.principle: Some combat aftermath originates not in threat but in having done, witnessed or been ordered into something that violated the person's moral framework — particularly when a legitimate authority was the source. Its presentation, its trajectory and what helps it differ from those of fear-based injury.
entries.example: Jonathan Shay's clinical work with Vietnam veterans in Achilles in Vietnam (1994) and Odysseus in America (2002) located the injury in betrayal of what is right by a legitimate authority; the subsequent moral-injury literature has developed the concept, while its boundary with post-traumatic stress disorder and its measurement remain disputed.
entries.application: Decide which injury the book's veteran has. Writing all combat aftermath as fear removes the category that most often applies to the characters who did something rather than survived something.

entries.name: Ground Shapes What Is Possible; It Does Not Decide What Happens
entries.description: Terrain constrains the options available to both sides and determines none of the outcome.
entries.principle: The same ground produces different results with different forces, doctrines and seasons. Terrain sets the menu — where movement is possible, what can be seen, where a position is worth holding — and everything after that is a matter of who is on it.
entries.example: The Ardennes was assessed as impassable to armour and was crossed by it; the same region produced three quite different campaigns in 1914, 1940 and 1944 with the ground unchanged.
entries.application: Use the ground to constrain choices, not to produce outcomes. Terrain determinism is the genre's favourite shortcut and it removes agency from both sides at once.

entries.name: The Map Lies, and It Lies in Known Directions
entries.description: Maps are out of date, drawn at a scale that hides what matters, and wrong about trafficability in predictable ways.
entries.principle: A map's errors are systematic rather than random: it is old, its scale conceals microterrain, and its assessments of what a road will carry were made for different vehicles. Commanders know this and plan around it, which is itself a source of error.
entries.example: The 1940 Ardennes roads were assessed as inadequate for armour and were not; Clausewitz had already noted the difference between the map and the country, and the problem long outlives paper.
entries.application: Give the map a specific, plausible error and let a decision rest on it. The reliable map is a modern reader's assumption imported into periods that never had one.

entries.name: Weather Produces Casualties, and It Takes Them From the Badly Supplied First
entries.description: Cold, wet and heat generate large numbers of losses in their own right, and the losses fall on whoever is worst equipped. Period-bound to the clothing and supply of the army concerned.
entries.principle: Weather is not atmosphere; it is a casualty-producing agent whose effects are unevenly distributed by logistics. Two armies in the same weather suffer differently, and the difference is boots, rotation and dry ground rather than hardiness.
entries.example: The US Army's cold-injury experience in the European winter of 1944–45, recorded in the official medical history volume on cold injury, generated very large numbers of non-battle casualties from trench foot and frostbite, concentrated where supply of footwear and rotation out of the line had failed.
entries.application: Cost the weather in people, and let the cost fall unevenly. Weather written as mood is the single easiest place to add real attrition to a book that has none.

entries.name: Mud and Season Set the Campaign Calendar
entries.description: Campaigns start and stop with the ground and the forage, and always have.
entries.principle: Movement is possible only in certain conditions, so wars run in seasons rather than continuously. The calendar is set by when the ground will carry transport and, before mechanisation, by when there was anything for the animals to eat.
entries.example: The rasputitsa halted movement on the Eastern Front twice a year between 1941 and 1944; the eighteenth-century campaigning season ended with the forage, which is why armies went into winter quarters rather than pressing an advantage.
entries.application: Put the campaign inside a season and let the season end it. A war that runs continuously through a year has removed the constraint that structured most campaigns in history.

entries.name: Battle, Campaign and War Run on Three Different Clocks
entries.description: The tempo of a firefight, of an operation and of a war are unrelated, and characters experience only the first — most of which is waiting.
entries.principle: A soldier lives at the tempo of minutes and hours; a campaign moves in weeks; a war moves in years. Narrating any one of them at another's speed distorts everything, and the dominant experience at the lowest level is not action but duration.
entries.example: The operational-art distinction between tactical, operational and strategic tempo is standard doctrine, and the near-universal veteran testimony about the ratio of boredom to terror describes what the lowest clock actually feels like.
entries.application: Choose which clock the book runs on and convert deliberately between them. Novels that narrate a war at the tempo of a firefight exhaust the reader; novels that narrate a firefight at the tempo of a war remove the reason anyone is frightened.

entries.name: Things Take Longer Than the Plan, and the Overrun Compounds
entries.description: Every timed military activity slips, and each slippage is inherited by everything scheduled behind it.
entries.principle: Friction expressed in time is cumulative rather than isolated. A relief-in-place that runs late delays the attack that follows it, which arrives after the supporting fire has been fired, which changes the outcome — and none of it requires anyone to have made a mistake.
entries.example: The observed slippage of H-hours, relief-in-place timings and river crossings is the ordinary condition of operations, and Clausewitz had already located it in the resistance of the medium rather than in incompetence.
entries.application: Build the schedule, then break it early and let the consequences propagate. A timetable that holds is the clearest sign that a book's war has no friction in it.

entries.name: A Siege Is a Clock, and the Two Kinds of Siege Run Different Clocks
entries.description: Encirclement converts a battle into an arithmetic problem that both sides can read — but the early-modern clock and the modern one are different mechanisms. Period-bound.
entries.principle: In the formal siege the clock is engineering: approach, sap, breach, and a set of conventions governing when surrender remains honourable. In the modern encirclement the clock is calories and ammunition, and there are no conventions. Treating these as the same form imports mercy rules into a situation that has none.
entries.example: Christopher Duffy's work on early-modern siege warfare describes the formal stages and the negotiated conventions attached to them; Stalingrad in 1942–43 and Sarajevo between 1992 and 1995 ran on supply arithmetic with the conventions absent.
entries.application: Establish which clock the siege runs on before writing a surrender scene. The honourable-terms convention belongs to a specific period and its transplantation is one of the genre's quieter anachronisms.

entries.name: Distance Multiplies the Defender and Divides the Attacker
entries.description: A force's usable strength falls with its distance from its base, and the same force is worth less the further it goes.
entries.principle: Every kilometre of separation from the source of supply consumes transport, garrison and security, so nominal strength and effective strength diverge as an advance lengthens. The defender fighting close to his own base does not pay this and is proportionally stronger for the same numbers.
entries.example: Kenneth Boulding's loss-of-strength gradient in Conflict and Defense (1962) formalises the effect, and van Creveld's operational-reach material supplies the mechanism behind it.
entries.application: Discount an expeditionary force's strength by its distance. Writing a deployed formation at its nominal strength is the arithmetic error behind most implausible campaigns in fiction.

entries.name: The Wound Is Not the Calibre
entries.description: What a projectile does to a body is a function of energy, yaw, the tissue it passes through and how long until care — not of the number stamped on the cartridge.
entries.principle: Calibre alone predicts wound severity poorly. The same round produces very different injuries depending on what it strikes, whether it tumbles, and how far the casualty is from surgical care, which is why identical weapons produce different casualty profiles in different theatres.
entries.example: The wound-ballistics literature in the Borden Institute volumes sets out the distinction between temporary and permanent cavity and the weak predictive value of calibre, which is the technical basis for treating so-called knockdown power as a fiction.
entries.application: Write the wound from the anatomy and the evacuation time, not from the weapon's specification. Calibre determinism is where technical enthusiasm most often replaces knowledge in this genre.

entries.name: Indirect Fire Is a Procedure, and the Procedure Is the Weapon
entries.description: What made artillery decisive was an organisational system for calling and massing it, not improvements to guns. Period-bound: mature from roughly 1941–42.
entries.principle: Artillery's effect depends on a call procedure with a delay and an error budget, and on an organisation able to concentrate dispersed batteries on one point at short notice. Close air support is the same problem carrying a worse coordination penalty.
entries.example: The US fire-direction centre and the British regimental fire-control system allowed massed battalion and divisional fire on call — an organisational innovation rather than a technical one. The parallel development of forward air control from the Second World War to the modern joint terminal attack controller followed the same path, and recurrent close-air-support fratricide marks where it fails.
entries.application: Give artillery a call procedure, a delay and an error, and let a character wait through it. Artillery as an offstage noise removes the system, and an airstrike written as a button removes the coordination that is the whole difficulty.

entries.name: Air Power Promises More Than It Delivers and Delivers More Than Its Critics Allow
entries.description: Every generation has claimed air power would be decisive and every generation has been partly right and largely wrong. Contested; the literature supports neither extreme.
entries.principle: The recurring claim is that striking an enemy's cities, will or leadership will produce capitulation without a land campaign, and the recurring result is partial. The argument in the scholarship is about which mechanism, if any, actually coerces.
entries.example: Douhet's interwar claims set the pattern; the US Strategic Bombing Survey returned mixed findings; Robert Pape argued in Bombing to Win (1996) that of punishment, risk, decapitation and denial, only denial reliably coerces, and that strategic bombing is rarely the best route to denial. The thesis is disputed in both directions in the subsequent literature, and the pack records the dispute rather than settling it.
entries.application: Decide what the book's air campaign is supposed to achieve and let it partly fail. Air power written as decisive or as useless both take a position the evidence does not support.

entries.name: Armour Without Combined Arms Is a Casualty
entries.description: The tank is one arm of a system, and separated from infantry, artillery and engineers it is a target rather than a weapon.
entries.principle: Armour's protection is bought by mobility and mutual support; in close country or a city, without dismounted infantry to see for it and clear the ground it cannot cover, it is blind and fixed. The weapon is the combination, not the vehicle.
entries.example: Villers-Bocage in 1944 demonstrated what armour in close country without infantry is worth, and mechanised columns entering Grozny in 1994–95 without dismounted infantry produced the modern textbook case, documented in the Russian lessons-learned literature that followed.
entries.application: Put infantry, engineers and artillery around the armour or explain their absence. The tank as an invulnerable object moving through a battle is the genre's most persistent equipment error.

entries.name: The Submarine's Power Is the Threat, and the Answer Was Arithmetic
entries.description: Commerce raiding works by forcing an enemy to reorganise an entire ocean, and it was defeated by statistics rather than by duels.
entries.principle: A submarine's effect is measured by what its potential presence compels — convoying, escorting, routing, delay — rather than by tonnage sunk. The counter is correspondingly systemic: convoy concentrates shipping so that the ocean is empty and attackers must come where the escorts are.
entries.example: The Battle of the Atlantic turned on the convoy system's inversion of the problem, and P. M. S. Blackett's operational-research group produced a series of results — convoy size, depth-charge settings, aircraft colour schemes — that solved tactical problems tactics had not.
entries.application: Let the threat do the work and let the solution be unglamorous. Naval war written as a sequence of duels misses both the mechanism and the fact that the war-winning ideas were statistics rather than inspiration.

entries.name: The New Weapon Is Overestimated at Introduction and Underestimated in Its Second-Order Effects
entries.description: A novel capability's direct effect is always smaller than promised, and its effect on how everyone else must operate is always larger.
entries.principle: The direct claim — this will end the war, this will make defence impossible — fails. What actually changes is that every other actor reorganises around the new thing: formations disperse, procedures change, whole categories of previous practice become unusable.
entries.example: The machine gun before 1914, the tank in 1916, the aircraft carrier before 1941, precision munitions after 1991 and armed drones after 2001 all follow the same curve, and the military-innovation literature treats the pattern as the norm rather than the exception.
entries.application: Let the wonder weapon disappoint and then change everything anyway. Fiction usually gets this exactly backwards, granting a large direct effect and no adaptation by anyone else.

entries.name: Counterinsurgency Force Ratios Were Doctrine and Were Then Removed From Doctrine
entries.description: The familiar troops-per-population figure entered US doctrine with a caveat, was dropped, and was then removed entirely — and its validity is disputed. Contested.
entries.principle: Insurgency is a system with a logic rather than a background hostility, but the quantitative rules once attached to countering it did not survive scrutiny. A number that appears in commentary as a law of counterinsurgency has a specific and short doctrinal life.
entries.example: James Quinlivan's figure of twenty counterinsurgents per thousand inhabitants was adopted in US Field Manual 3-24 in 2006 with an explicit situational caveat; Joint Publication 3-24 in 2009 dropped the number and stated that no fixed ratio ensures success; the 2013–14 revisions removed force-density references altogether. The classical counterinsurgency model associated with David Galula's Counterinsurgency Warfare (1964) is itself contested in the modern quantitative literature.
entries.application: Do not put the ratio in a character's mouth as settled doctrine unless the scene is set in the years it was doctrine. It is a useful marker of exactly when a book's professional dialogue is set.

entries.name: Ground Held Is Not Ground Controlled
entries.description: Control is a function of presence over time, and the map with coloured territory on it describes something that does not exist in irregular war.
entries.principle: Clearing an area and holding it are different operations requiring different force levels and different durations, and the recurring failure is to perform the first and report it as the second. Territory changes hands at night without a shot being fired anywhere.
entries.example: The clear-hold-build formulation in counterinsurgency doctrine encodes the distinction precisely because clearing without holding is the standard failure; the efficacy of the doctrine as a whole remains disputed.
entries.application: Ask who is present at night. A book that shows a map with territory on it is describing a conventional war, and if the war it is describing is irregular, the map is a character's illusion rather than a fact.

entries.name: Technological Asymmetry Wins Engagements and Does Not End Wars
entries.description: The materially superior side generally wins the fighting and frequently loses the war, and why that happens is disputed.
entries.principle: Overwhelming technical advantage reliably produces tactical victory and does not reliably produce political outcomes. The pattern is consistent enough to be treated as a rule; the explanations offered for it are not settled.
entries.example: The recurrence runs from colonial campaigns through Vietnam, Afghanistan and Iraq. Andrew Mack's asymmetric-conflict work and Ivan Arreguín-Toft's How the Weak Win Wars (2005) offer competing causal accounts — relative interest and political vulnerability against strategic interaction — and the pack records the pattern as established and the explanation as contested.
entries.application: Let the book's superior force win everything and achieve nothing. The technology-solves-it plot is contradicted by the whole record of the last century of irregular war.

entries.name: The Distance Kill Changes the Operator's Experience Without Removing It
entries.description: Remote crews show substantially lower rates of post-traumatic symptoms than deployed ground troops, alongside high rates of burnout and fatigue. Contested in its popular form.
entries.principle: Killing at distance does not produce the same injury as killing in person, and it does not produce no injury. The documented burden is heavily occupational — shift work, manning shortfalls, and the compression of combat and domestic life into a single day — rather than a replica of ground-combat trauma.
entries.example: Chappelle and colleagues' survey work on US Air Force remotely-piloted-aircraft crews, published in the Journal of Anxiety Disorders (2014) and extended in later studies, found post-traumatic symptom rates in the low single-digit percentages, well below deployed ground-combat rates, together with high occupational burnout. The popular claim that drone crews suffer post-traumatic stress just as deployed troops do is contested by this evidence, and the pack states both the claim and the finding.
entries.application: Write the specific burden rather than either cliché. The joystick warrior who feels nothing and the drone operator with a ground soldier's trauma are both corrected by the same data, and the true version — going home for dinner after a strike — is stranger than either.

entries.name: The Law Governs How War Is Fought and Says Nothing About Whether It Should Have Begun
entries.description: The justice of a cause confers no latitude in conduct, and most modern conflicts fall under a much thinner body of rules than the familiar one.
entries.principle: The separation between the law governing resort to force and the law governing conduct in it is structural. A just cause licenses nothing, an unjust one forbids nothing additional, and both sides are bound identically. Separately, the treaty machinery most people picture applies fully only to conflicts between states.
entries.example: The International Committee of the Red Cross sets out the separation directly in its material on the rules of war. Common Article 3 provides the floor for conflicts that are not between states, and the treaty coverage above that floor is markedly thinner — which matters because most conflicts since 1945 have been of that kind.
entries.application: Establish which body of law the book's war falls under before anyone invokes a rule. Applying full prisoner-of-war machinery to a civil war or an insurgency is a common error that changes what every character is entitled to.

entries.name: Distinction Is a Bright Line; Proportionality Is a Judgement Made in Advance
entries.description: Of the three operative principles, only the prohibition on targeting civilians is categorical — and proportionality is assessed on what was expected, not on what happened.
entries.principle: Distinction, proportionality and precaution are not three versions of one rule. Distinction is absolute. Proportionality weighs expected incidental civilian harm against anticipated concrete and direct military advantage, prospectively — so a terrible outcome may have been lawful and a bloodless one may not.
entries.example: The ICRC's customary-law material and its guidance on the rules of war set out all three, and the prospective character of the proportionality assessment is explicit in it. That the judgement is inherently arguable is a property of the law rather than a defect in it.
entries.application: Have the argument in the book take place before the strike, not after it. The scene in which a lawful attack is retrospectively condemned by its result is dramatically obvious and legally backwards, and the correct version is more uncomfortable.

entries.name: A Person Becomes Protected at a Defined Moment
entries.description: The point at which someone is out of the fight is specified in law, not left to the judgement of the person pointing the weapon.
entries.principle: Surrender, capture, or wounds or sickness rendering a person defenceless place him outside the permissible target set immediately and unconditionally. The law is precise here in a way it is not elsewhere, and the precision is what makes the point-blank scene a legal question rather than an emotional one.
entries.example: Common Article 3 and Article 41 of Additional Protocol I define the condition of being out of combat and the protection attaching to it, and the ICRC's material states the moment plainly.
entries.application: Let the characters know the rule and let the scene turn on it. Fiction habitually plays this as an ambiguity, and the ambiguity in the scene is psychological rather than legal.

entries.name: Direct Participation in Hostilities Is the Law's Most Contested Term
entries.description: Civilians lose protection only for such time as they take a direct part in hostilities, and what counts is genuinely unsettled. Contested.
entries.principle: The rule is clear in form and disputed in application: the loss of protection is temporary, tied to specific acts, and does not follow from sympathy, support or association. Where the boundary sits — the driver, the lookout, the man storing weapons — is argued.
entries.example: The ICRC's Interpretive Guidance on Direct Participation in Hostilities (2009) sets out one position, and sustained state and academic disagreement with it constitutes the other; the dispute is live and the pack does not settle it.
entries.application: Write the uncertainty into the decision rather than resolving it offstage. The shortcut in which someone was helping them and was therefore a target is exactly the reasoning the disputed term exists to discipline.

entries.name: The Prisoner Is a Legal Category, a Procedure, and a Burden
entries.description: A prisoner of war is not a criminal for having fought; capture is a defined sequence; and the burden of it falls on the unit least able to carry it, at the moment of highest danger.
entries.principle: Lawful participation in hostilities is not a crime, so captivity is not punishment and release follows the end of active hostilities; a prisoner may be prosecuted only for unlawful acts. Practically, taking and moving prisoners drains the assaulting element at the moment it can least spare people.
entries.example: The Third Geneva Convention establishes combatant immunity, the limits of prosecution and the release requirement; the capture-to-camp chain is standard doctrine in every modern army. The pack states the pattern of where violations have clustered and adjudicates no individual incident.
entries.application: Do not cut from surrender to camp. The dangerous interval is the one the book skips, and it is dangerous for structural reasons a scene can dramatise without accusing anyone.

entries.name: The Manifestly Unlawful Order Is Rare in the Form Fiction Gives It
entries.description: Obedience is no defence to an order that is manifestly unlawful — and the explicit atrocity order is unusual, while the ambiguous order in a permissive climate is common.
entries.principle: The legal standard turns on the word manifest, and the orders that produce atrocities are usually not manifest at all. They are ambiguous, deniable, delivered in a climate that has already communicated what is expected, and they leave the decision with the person who has to act on them.
entries.example: The superior-orders provisions in the Nuremberg Charter, in Article 33 of the Rome Statute, and in national military law all set the standard at manifest unlawfulness, and the military-justice literature is clear that this is a high threshold.
entries.application: Write the ambiguous order and the permissive climate rather than the explicit one. The scene in which an officer orders a massacre in plain terms is the version that almost never happens and the one that lets everyone else off.

entries.name: Why Ordinary Men Commit Atrocity Is Disputed, and the Dispute Is the Card
entries.description: Atrocity is generally committed by unremarkable people under specifiable conditions; which conditions do the work is exactly what scholars disagree about. Contested; real events and real dead, analysed at the level of the scholarship only.
entries.principle: Both available shortcuts are wrong. The monster explanation is contradicted by the evidence about who these people were; the anyone-would explanation is a specific scholarly position rather than a settled finding, and it is disputed by scholars working from the same documents.
entries.example: Christopher Browning's Ordinary Men (1992) and Daniel Goldhagen's Hitler's Willing Executioners (1996) reach different conclusions about Reserve Police Battalion 101 from the same postwar interrogation records — Browning locating the mechanism in situational pressure, conformity and incremental commitment, Goldhagen in a specific eliminationist ideology. The United States Holocaust Memorial Museum's occasional paper on the exchange documents the debate. The pack states that the mechanism is disputed and adopts neither account.
entries.application: Choose a mechanism knowingly and let the book be answerable for the choice. A novel that explains atrocity by monstrousness has taken a position the evidence contradicts, and one that explains it by circumstance has taken a contested side while appearing not to take one.

entries.name: Concealment of a War Crime Is Paperwork, Not Conspiracy
entries.description: Suppression follows an administrative pattern — a plausible initial report, a failed immediate investigation, and outsiders forcing the matter years later.
entries.principle: The mechanism is institutional rather than conspiratorial. An initial report is filed in a form the system accepts, the investigation nearest the event fails because interested parties conduct it, and the matter surfaces only when someone outside the chain takes it elsewhere.
entries.example: My Lai in March 1968 was initially reported as an enemy body count; the immediate command investigation failed; Ronald Ridenhour's letters brought it to people outside the chain; and the Peers Inquiry, reporting to the Department of the Army in 1970, treated the suppression itself as an institutional failure. Questions of individual culpability are settled or contested in ways this pack does not adjudicate.
entries.application: Write the concealment as filing rather than as a meeting. The cover-up staged as a conspiracy of villains is both less accurate and structurally reassuring, because it implies the institution would have worked if the villains were removed.

entries.name: Occupation Is an Administrative Condition With Duties Attached
entries.description: Occupation begins as a matter of fact whether or not it is declared, and it imposes positive obligations rather than merely permitting control.
entries.principle: An occupying power must restore and ensure public order and civil life, and may not alter the territory's legal order except as permitted. Occupation is a governing task with duties, and they begin the moment effective control exists, whatever anyone calls it.
entries.example: Articles 42 and 43 of the Hague Regulations of 1907 and the Fourth Geneva Convention establish both the factual test for occupation and the obligations that follow from it, as the ICRC's material sets out.
entries.application: Make the occupier responsible for rubbish collection, courts and food as well as checkpoints. Occupation written purely as a security posture omits the part that generates most of the resentment and most of the plot.

entries.name: The Ceasefire and the Tribunal Are Two Endings That Are Not Endings
entries.description: A ceasefire is a technical instrument that usually fails in specifiable ways, and a tribunal arrives years later to answer a different question from the one the participants were asking.
entries.principle: A suspension of arms, an armistice and a peace treaty are different instruments, and ceasefires fail through undefined lines, absent monitoring and spoiler factions. The tribunal works on documents to a legal standard and produces a finding about liability, not an account of what happened.
entries.example: The distinctions between the instruments are standard in the laws-of-war literature, and the recurring failure modes are documented in the conflict-termination scholarship, including Virginia Fortna's work on ceasefire durability. Nuremberg and Tokyo, the tribunals for the former Yugoslavia and for Rwanda, and the International Criminal Court all illustrate the reshaping that evidentiary standards, defendant selection and the lapse of time impose on the question.
entries.application: Refuse both endings the closure they appear to offer. The ceasefire that ends a novel and the trial that resolves it are the two most available false conclusions in the genre, and the record supports neither.

entries.name: The Gap Audit
entries.description: The pack's first diagnostic. Name the distance between the event this book represents and the representation, and decide what the book will do about it.
entries.principle: Every war book stands at some distance from the thing it represents, and the distance is not a defect to be minimised. The question is whether the book knows where it is standing and lets the reader feel it, or whether it presents its account as though no gap existed.
entries.example: Tim O'Brien's The Things They Carried (1990) makes the unauditability of its own war stories the subject rather than a problem to be solved; Gert Ledig's Die Stalinorgel (1955) admits the gap by refusing the reader any vantage from which the action would cohere.
entries.application: Before drafting, write one sentence naming what this book cannot reach, and keep it where you can see it. If the answer is that the book reaches everything, the audit has failed and the rest of the diagnostic block will fail with it.

entries.name: Accuracy Is Not the Same as Honesty
entries.description: A scrupulously researched account can close the gap dishonestly, and an invented one can hold it open.
entries.principle: Getting the equipment, the dates and the order of battle right does not discharge the obligation, because the falsification the genre commits is not usually factual. It is the conversion of an incoherent experience into a coherent account, which correct detail makes more persuasive rather than less.
entries.example: The most technically meticulous military fiction frequently produces the most confident battles, because the accuracy of the furniture underwrites the reader's trust in the shape of the whole; the research is real and the effect is a war that made sense to the people in it.
entries.application: Separate the two questions in revision. Ask what the book got right and then ask, independently, whether the reader finishes a scene understanding it better than any participant could have — those are different audits and only the second is this one.

entries.name: The Legibility Trap
entries.description: Making combat comprehensible is the genre's central technical act and its central falsification, and the clarifying sentence is also the exciting one.
entries.principle: Combat as experienced is fragmentary, sensorily overloaded and largely invisible; narrative is ordered, compressed and clear. Every craft decision trades one against the other, and the trade runs one way by default because clarity reads better on the page.
entries.example: Stephen Crane's The Red Badge of Courage (1895) keeps its protagonist inside a battle he never sees whole, and the prose declines the clarity that would have made the action easier to follow.
entries.application: Audit a battle scene for how much the reader understands that no character does. Some of that is craft; past a point it is the book telling the reader that war can be followed, which is the thing it cannot do honestly.

entries.name: When the War Is Made to Mean
entries.description: The first of the two symmetrical failures: violence rendered as meaningful, redemptive, clarifying or purchased.
entries.principle: Glorification in modern war fiction rarely looks like flag-waving. It looks like significance: a death that teaches the survivors something, a unit whose losses buy cohesion, an ordeal that produces a better person. Each of these closes the gap by making the violence pay for something.
entries.example: The unit-as-family structure is where this operates most invisibly, because the affection is real and the losses are grievous — and the book still ends up asserting that the deaths bought the bond that makes them grievable.
entries.application: List what each death in the manuscript buys. Where a loss purchases growth, unity or meaning, either remove the purchase or make the reader see the book making it — the honest version is usually that the death was structurally wasted, as most were.

entries.name: When the War Is Made Consumable
entries.description: The second symmetrical failure: suffering rendered at maximum intensity for the reader's harrowing, with horror standing in for a claim.
entries.principle: Atrocity tourism does not announce itself as entertainment. It presents as unflinching, and it is recognisable by escalation without argument — each scene worse than the last because the book needs the reader's response to keep rising, not because the material demands it.
entries.example: The siege and genocide forms are where this is hardest to see, because every individual escalation is defensible as accuracy, and the pattern only becomes visible across a whole book.
entries.application: Chart the intensity curve across the manuscript. If the second half is more harrowing than the first and nothing in the material required that, the escalation belongs to the reader rather than to the war, and it is the same failure as glorification wearing the opposite face.

entries.category: Sensorium, Range and the Interiority Budget
entries.name: The Interiority Ledger
entries.description: The second diagnostic. Who gets rendered from inside, at what depth, for how long — and who is only ever seen from outside.
entries.principle: Interiority is finite and its distribution is an argument about whose consciousness counts. Four positions are systematically under-rendered in this genre — the civilian, the enemy, the prisoner and the dead — and a book that leaves all four outside has made a claim it did not intend to defend.
entries.example: Len Deighton's Bomber (1970) spends interiority on the German village beneath the raid as well as on the crew above it, and the structural decision does more moral work than any statement in the book could.
entries.application: Count the pages of interior access by position, not by character. The ledger is usually more lopsided than the writer believes, and the correction is structural rather than a matter of adding sympathetic lines.

entries.category: Sensorium, Range and the Interiority Budget
entries.name: The Civilian Is the Subject, Not the Weather
entries.description: Write the non-combatant first. In a genre whose obligation is to the people it happened to, civilians are the majority of those people and the default casualty of the pack's own vocabulary.
entries.principle: Combat, command and friction are a vocabulary that selects combatants, and a book built in that vocabulary will render civilians as conditions — bombed, displaced, occupied, endured — rather than as consciousnesses with their own war. The correction is to draft them first and extend to the soldiers, not the reverse.
entries.example: Elizabeth Bowen's The Heat of the Day (1948) makes wartime London a state of consciousness rather than a setting; Ghassan Kanafani's Rijāl fī al-shams (1963) gives displacement its own interior logic rather than treating it as the aftermath of someone else's battle.
entries.application: Draft the civilian scenes before the combat scenes, in the civilian's terms, and let the soldiers arrive into a world that already has interiority in it. A civilian who exists to be affected is weather, and the book's claim about what it owes has quietly excluded most of the people it owes it to.

entries.category: Sensorium, Range and the Interiority Budget
entries.name: The Enemy Rendered Only From Outside
entries.description: Declining to interiorise the enemy is a choice with consequences, not a neutral absence.
entries.principle: An adversary who is never rendered from inside becomes a condition of the environment, and the book has argued — without saying so — that his consciousness is not of the same kind. The opposite error is the false symmetry that grants him a mirrored interiority and flatters the reader into thinking the matter settled.
entries.example: Vercors's Le Silence de la mer (1942) puts a cultivated occupier in the house and grants him substantial presence while refusing him the sympathy that presence usually buys, which is a third position between the two errors.
entries.application: Decide explicitly whether the enemy will be interiorised anywhere in the book, and if not, know what you have asserted. The decision is more defensible when made than when arrived at by default.

entries.category: Sensorium, Range and the Interiority Budget
entries.name: The Prisoner, the Wounded and the Dead
entries.description: Three positions the genre routinely converts into objects — the captured, the casualty and the corpse.
entries.principle: The prisoner is the person the narrative has stopped needing, the wounded man is frequently a problem for other characters rather than a consciousness, and the dead become terrain. Each conversion is a small, near-invisible instance of the same failure the pack's whole claim is about.
entries.example: The captivity form makes the first unavoidable and is therefore the place to study it; the guard and the prisoner are in daily contact and every POW novel decides, usually silently, which of them has an inside.
entries.application: Find the manuscript's wounded and check whether their pain is theirs or is the scene's obstacle. The corpse used as description is the cheapest version of this and the easiest to catch in revision.

entries.category: Sensorium, Range and the Interiority Budget
entries.name: Choosing the Range at Which the War Is Narrated
entries.description: Every range — the individual, the section, the battalion, the theatre — carries some truths and forecloses others, and the choice is not a matter of scale alone.
entries.principle: The soldier's-eye view delivers phenomenology and cannot deliver causation; the theatre view delivers causation and cannot deliver what anything felt like. Moving between them is legitimate, but each transition grants the reader knowledge someone in the book has just been denied.
entries.example: Vasily Grossman's Жизнь и судьба, completed by 1959 and published in Switzerland in 1980, moves between ranges deliberately, and the discontinuity between what the reader knows at each level is part of what the novel is arguing.
entries.application: Mark every range change in the outline and ask what the reader gains that the characters do not. An unmarked drift upward is how a book acquires an omniscience it never decided to claim.

entries.name: What the Operational Summary Destroys
entries.description: The third diagnostic, in its positive form: name what the book's form carries that a report, a citation or an after-action summary could not.
entries.principle: War generates its own official prose — the situation report, the citation, the unit history — and that prose is a complete account by its own standards. If a novel's content survives translation into it without loss, the novel has not yet found a reason to be a novel.
entries.example: The citation for gallantry is the sharpest test case, because it narrates the same event the book narrates, in a form designed to be unarguable, and everything it removes is the material the fiction exists to carry.
entries.application: Write the after-action report for the book's central action, in its proper register, and compare. What is missing from the report is the book's actual subject, and anything the report captures fully is doing less work than it appears to.

entries.name: Rendering Chaos Without Becoming Unreadable
entries.description: Confusion has to be constructed, and the construction has a budget the reader will not exceed.
entries.principle: A scene that is genuinely as confusing as combat is unreadable, and a scene the reader follows easily is a lie about combat. The workable position is local incoherence inside global orientation: the reader knows where they are in the book while the characters do not know where they are in the fight.
entries.example: Ledig's Die Stalinorgel (1955) pushes as far toward genuine incoherence as the form allows and demonstrates both the technique and its limit.
entries.application: Give the reader a stable frame — a place, a person, a clock — and let everything inside it break. Disorientation without a frame reads as bad writing rather than as chaos, which is why the honest version so often gets revised away.

entries.name: Duration, Waiting and Boredom as Material
entries.description: Most of a war is waiting, and the genre's structures are built to skip it.
entries.principle: Narrative compresses toward event, and the compression removes the dominant experience of military life. Duration is not dead time to be summarised; it is the condition against which the events mean anything, and a book that cuts to the engagements has changed the ratio that defines the subject.
entries.example: The captivity form has no choice but to solve this, which is why it is the best place to learn it — the alternative, inventing an escape, is the same book abandoning the problem.
entries.application: Keep at least one long passage of nothing happening and make it carry weight. If every scene in the manuscript is an event, the book is describing a war that consisted entirely of its exceptional moments.

entries.name: The Battle Scene's Vantage Problem
entries.description: A set-piece action has to be narrated from somewhere, and the somewhere decides what the battle means.
entries.principle: There is no neutral position from which to describe an engagement. A vantage inside it delivers incomprehension; a vantage above it delivers a shape nobody experienced; alternating between them grants the reader a composite view no participant possessed. The choice is the scene's argument.
entries.example: Michael Shaara's The Killer Angels (1974) narrates a documented battle from both commands and accepts the composite view as the price of its subject; the historical-fiction pack cards the same work for a different question, about whose account survived to be dramatised.
entries.application: Fix the vantage before writing the scene and note what it costs. Vantage chosen shot by shot for maximum effect produces a battle that is legible because it was assembled from the best view of each moment.

entries.name: The Omniscient Overview and What It Falsifies
entries.description: The panoramic narrator is the genre's most efficient device and its most reliable source of retrospective omniscience.
entries.principle: An overview delivers causation cheaply, and it imports the historian's hindsight into a moment that did not contain it. Decisions become explicable, failures become foreseeable, and the reader acquires a clarity whose absence was the whole condition the characters were operating under.
entries.example: The specialist collection's rules on the commander's information horizon and on reasoning from a biased sample are the technical basis for this card: a narrator who can see the battle has contradicted the conditions under which it was fought.
entries.application: If the book uses an overview, date it — make the reader feel that the clarity belongs to afterwards. Undated omniscience presents hindsight as contemporaneous and turns tragedy into stupidity.

entries.name: Standing, and the Argument About It
entries.description: The fourth diagnostic. Who is entitled to write this, and how the book answers a question that is genuinely disputed among serious writers, including among veterans.
entries.principle: The pack's boundary deliberately excludes standing from the definition of the genre, because a craft question should not be settled by a credential. But the question is live, it is argued in good faith on both sides, and a book that has not located its own position within that argument has taken one by default.
entries.example: Stephen Crane wrote the American canon's founding combat novel without having seen a war; the memoir-adjacent tradition rests on the opposite claim. Both positions are held by serious practitioners, and the disagreement is not resolvable by argument from either example.
entries.application: Locate the book's position in the dispute rather than assuming it away, and let the text rather than the jacket copy carry it. A claim to authority made only in the paratext is one the prose has not paid for.

entries.name: Testimony and Fiction That Borrows Its Authority
entries.description: Fiction can adopt the register of testimony and receive its epistemic privilege without accepting its constraints.
entries.principle: Testimony claims to report; fiction claims the licence to invent. Prose that sounds like testimony collects the first while retaining the second, and the reader has no way to audit which is operating in any sentence. The form is legitimate; taking the privilege without acknowledging the borrowing is not.
entries.example: O'Brien's The Things They Carried (1990) makes the impossibility of auditing it the explicit subject; Jerzy Kosiński's The Painted Bird (1965) is a contested-provenance case in which the relationship between the book and the author's own account has been disputed, which the pack records without adjudicating.
entries.application: Decide what the book claims about its own truth, and say so inside the book. The composite character, the compressed timeline and the invented incident are all available to fiction and all become something else when the prose is asking to be believed as report.

entries.name: The Real Unit, the Real Operation, the Real Dead
entries.description: Naming a real formation or a real action attaches the book's invention to people who existed and to records that can be checked. Sensitive material: named plainly and analysed as craft.
entries.principle: Once a real unit is named, every invented act is attributed to identifiable people. The book has acquired a factual liability it cannot discharge by disclaimer, and the choice between a real designation and an invented one is a substantive craft decision rather than a matter of flavour.
entries.example: The military-adventure and technothriller traditions attach invented actions to real formations as a matter of routine, and the historical-fiction pack's cards on real people as characters cover the adjacent question of the named individual.
entries.application: Choose deliberately between the real designation and the invented one, and if the real one is used, keep the invented conduct inside what the record will bear. Verify the unit, the operation and the dates as you would verify a publication date.

entries.name: The Descendant and the Surviving Comrade Are Readers
entries.description: For most wars a novel can be written about, some of the people it happened to — or their children — will read it.
entries.principle: This is the structural fact that distinguishes war fiction's ethical position from historical fiction's. The archive problem is about silence; this is about presence. The relevant test is not whether a depiction is defensible in the abstract but whether it is answerable to someone who was there.
entries.example: The civil-war form presses this hardest, because the book is read inside its own dispute by survivors of both sides; Adichie's Half of a Yellow Sun (2006) and Khoury's Gate of the Sun (1998) are both written in that condition.
entries.application: Identify who is still alive to read the book before drafting the scenes that would matter most to them. This is not a veto and should not be used as one — it is a specification of the audience the book is actually answerable to.

entries.name: Aestheticisation Is a Craft Failure, Not a Failure of Taste
entries.description: Making suffering beautiful is a technical error with a technical description, and treating it as a matter of decorum lets it survive revision.
entries.principle: The problem is not that beautiful prose about atrocity is impolite. It is that the aesthetic response displaces the response the material calls for, and the reader leaves the scene having had an experience the event cannot support. The failure is in what the sentence does to the reader, which is a craft question with a craft answer.
entries.example: The child-narrator device is the clearest instance, because incomprehension supplies lyricism at no cost to the writer, and the resulting prose is frequently beautiful in ways the child could not have produced.
entries.application: Find the manuscript's most admired sentences about the worst material and ask what they leave the reader feeling. If the answer is chiefly the pleasure of the writing, the sentence is doing the opposite of what the book needs, however good it is.

entries.name: Staging an Action the Reader Can Hold
entries.description: The technical construction of a combat scene: what to establish before the shooting, and what the reader must be able to keep track of once it starts.
entries.principle: A reader can hold roughly one geography, one objective and a small number of named people through an action, and everything beyond that is lost. The work of a combat scene is done before it begins, in what has been established well enough to survive the confusion.
entries.example: The small-unit tradition solves this by establishing the ground and the ensemble at length and then breaking both, which is why its actions remain followable while its characters are lost.
entries.application: Establish the ground, the objective and the people before the first round, then let all three degrade. A scene that has to explain its geography during the fighting has put the exposition where the reader cannot receive it.

entries.name: The Campaign's Shape Is Not the Novel's Shape
entries.description: Wars do not have three acts, and imposing narrative structure on a campaign is where most war novels quietly become something else.
entries.principle: A campaign's actual shape is long preparation, brief violence, longer aftermath, and an ending determined elsewhere. Novel structure wants rising action and a climax, and the two are incompatible enough that one has to give — usually the campaign, silently.
entries.example: The satiric tradition solves it by refusing narrative progression altogether; the small-unit tradition solves it with attrition, which produces a shape without requiring a climax.
entries.application: Decide which structure governs and pay for the choice openly. A campaign bent into three acts has acquired a climactic engagement that the war did not have, and the reader will take the shape as a claim about the war.

entries.name: The Training-to-Front Structure and What It Assumes
entries.description: The genre's most reliable opening — induction, training, deployment, contact — carries an argument about transformation that the book may not intend.
entries.principle: The structure implies that the war is something the protagonist is prepared for and then encounters, and that preparation and encounter can be compared. That comparison is the form's whole engine, and it also quietly asserts that becoming a soldier is a completed process with a before and an after.
entries.example: The structure is old enough to be nearly invisible and is used by books whose politics are entirely opposed to one another, which is evidence that it carries an argument independent of what the author puts into it.
entries.application: If the book uses the structure, decide what the training section is for beyond delay. If the answer is only that the reader needs to meet the characters, the section is doing structural work whose content the book has not chosen.

entries.name: The Return Structure and Its Flashback Problem
entries.description: A book about aftermath must decide how much war to show, and every flashback risks converting the aftermath into a delivery mechanism for combat.
entries.principle: Aftermath has no antagonist and no forward pressure, so the form reaches for the war to supply both. The more vivid the flashbacks, the more the present-tense material reads as the frame around them, and the book becomes a combat novel with a domestic wrapper.
entries.example: Rebecca West's The Return of the Soldier (1918) works almost entirely in the domestic present; Larry Heinemann's Paco's Story (1986) relocates the war into the narrating voice rather than into retrospective scenes.
entries.application: Count the pages. If the war scenes are where the prose comes alive, either cut them and find the aftermath's own pressure, or accept that the book is about the war and restructure honestly.

entries.name: Attrition as a Plot Engine
entries.description: An ensemble that is steadily reduced generates structure without requiring a climax — and the order of the reductions is an argument.
entries.principle: Attrition supplies forward motion, rising stakes and an ending without borrowing a three-act shape, which is why the genre reaches for it. But the schedule of deaths is authored, and whoever dies first, last and most meaningfully constitutes the book's position on whose life counted.
entries.example: The military-adventure series makes the problem visible at scale, because the protagonist's survival is guaranteed and the supporting cast is spent on a schedule the reader can chart across a dozen volumes.
entries.application: Chart the deaths and look for the pattern before a reviewer does. If the expendable are consistently the unnamed, the foreign or the recently introduced, that is the book's actual argument regardless of its stated one.

entries.name: Time Compression and What It Steals
entries.description: Summary is how a war novel survives its own timescale, and every compression removes duration, which is the material.
entries.principle: A book cannot render four years at scene length, so it compresses — and compression preferentially removes waiting, routine and repetition, which is precisely the dominant experience. The result is a war made of its exceptional moments, produced by a technique nobody chose for that purpose.
entries.example: The problem is structural rather than authorial: the same compression that makes a novel possible is the one that changes the ratio of boredom to terror, and it operates whether or not the writer notices.
entries.application: Compress deliberately and asymmetrically — summarise some action, render some waiting at length. Uniform compression always favours event, which means the default setting of the technique is already an argument about war.

entries.name: Writing Toward a Known Outcome
entries.description: Most war fiction is set in wars whose outcome the reader knows, and suspense has to come from something other than what happened.
entries.principle: The reader knows the war's result and frequently the battle's, so tension cannot rest on outcome. It has to rest on cost, on who specifically survives, and on the gap between what the characters believe is at stake and what the reader knows was.
entries.example: The historical-fiction pack owns the general form of this problem; the war version is narrower and harder, because the outcome the reader knows is usually also a death toll.
entries.application: Locate the book's suspense in cost rather than result. A book that generates tension by obscuring a historical outcome is asking the reader to unknow something and will lose the bet.

entries.name: The Ending That Refuses Resolution
entries.description: Wars end administratively, not narratively, and the two most available endings — the ceasefire and the trial — both offer a closure the record does not support.
entries.principle: An ending is a claim about what the war meant, and the genre supplies three cheap ones: the armistice, the verdict, and the return home. Each converts an unresolved condition into a completed action, which is the gap-closing failure performed at the structural level rather than the sentence level.
entries.example: The specialist collection's card on the ceasefire and the tribunal sets out why both are technically endings that end nothing; the displacement form has no available ending at all and is instructive for that reason.
entries.application: Draft the ending twice, once with closure and once without, and read both cold. The version that resists is usually the true one, and it is nearly always the one that revision has been trying to remove.

entries.name: Procedure and Jargon Without the Lecture
entries.description: Military language is the genre's fastest authenticity signal and its most common route to unreadability.
entries.principle: Jargon works when it is used rather than explained, and it fails in both directions: glossed in dialogue, it turns characters into instructors; unglossed and dense, it locks out every reader who is not already inside. The workable ratio is that the reader should understand the stakes without understanding the terms.
entries.example: The naval and technothriller traditions run at opposite ends of this — one trusting the reader to sail on partial comprehension, the other explaining its systems because the systems are the pleasure on offer.
entries.application: Let characters use terms correctly and never define them for each other. If a passage requires a glossary, move the meaning into the consequence rather than into an explanation.

entries.name: The Detail That Reads as Competence
entries.description: A small number of exactly right details buys more authority than volume, and volume actively costs.
entries.principle: Authority in this genre comes from specificity that a practitioner would remark on and a civilian would not think to invent — a weight, a smell, a routine, an irritation. Catalogue detail signals research; selected detail signals experience, and the two produce opposite effects at the same word count.
entries.example: Patrick O'Brian's Master and Commander (1969) delivers a fraction of what he knew and lets the rest operate as implied competence, which is why the technical material characterises rather than instructs.
entries.application: Cut the technical detail by two-thirds and keep the fraction a competent person would actually notice. The material that survives will carry more authority than the whole did.

entries.name: Getting the Equipment Right Without Becoming a Catalogue
entries.description: Weapons and equipment must be correct and must not become the subject, and the failure mode has a distinctive prose signature.
entries.principle: Equipment error destroys credibility with the readership most likely to review the book, and equipment enthusiasm destroys the book. The signature of the second is the specification appearing where the character's attention would not be — nobody under fire notices a designation.
entries.example: The specialist collection's rule that a wound is a function of energy, tissue and time to care rather than of calibre is the technical basis: precision about the number is frequently precision about the wrong variable.
entries.application: Write the equipment from the user's attention, not from the reference work. What a soldier notices about his weapon is its weight, its noise and whether it has stopped working.

entries.name: The Veteran Reader
entries.description: Someone who was there will read the book, and using that reader well is a specific practice distinct from either ignoring them or deferring to them.
entries.principle: A veteran reader catches procedural error, register error and the tonal wrongness a civilian cannot hear. They are not, and should not be treated as, an authority on what the book is permitted to say — one person's war is one person's war, and their objection to an interpretation is evidence rather than a verdict.
entries.example: The historical-fiction pack's card on the expert and the sensitivity reader covers the adjacent general practice; the war-specific difference is that the expert here is frequently also a survivor, and the two roles pull differently.
entries.application: Ask the veteran reader what is wrong, not whether the book is right. Separate their procedural corrections, which are usually decisive, from their interpretive objections, which are one testimony among the several the book is answerable to.

entries.name: Interviewing People Who Were There
entries.description: Combat testimony is unreliable in known directions, and the unreliability is itself material rather than a problem to be corrected.
entries.principle: Time estimates compress and dilate, sequences reorder, and accounts consolidate around the version that has been told before. None of this makes the testimony false; it makes it a record of how the event was survived rather than of how it occurred, which is frequently the more useful thing.
entries.example: The specialist collection records that nobody in a firefight knows how long it lasted, and combat interview practice has treated this as a known property of the source since the method began.
entries.application: Collect the account and its shape, and treat contradiction between two veterans of the same action as data rather than as an error to resolve. The historical-fiction pack owns the general source-reliability method; this is its living-witness case.

entries.name: Reading After-Action Reports and Unit Histories
entries.description: The war's own paperwork is the densest available source and it lies in characteristic directions.
entries.principle: An after-action report is written to a purpose — to justify, to instruct, to account — and each purpose deforms the record predictably. Casualty returns understate, citations dramatise, unit histories are written by survivors for survivors, and the absence of a report is itself information.
entries.example: The historical-fiction pack's specialist collection covers the general principle that every document lies in a characteristic direction; the war version has a specific set of documents whose deformations are well known and can be read through.
entries.application: Learn what each document type was for before mining it for detail. The report's silences and its enthusiasms are both usable once the purpose behind them is known.

entries.name: The Author's Note and What It Must Carry
entries.description: Where a book has used real units, real operations or real dead, the note is where the invention is declared — and it cannot retroactively license what the prose asserted.
entries.principle: The note's function is to tell the reader where the record ends and the invention begins, in enough detail to be checkable. It is not a disclaimer that converts an unfair depiction into a fair one, and a note that apologises for the book's method is evidence that the method needed changing.
entries.example: The historical-fiction pack cards the author's note as a general contract; the war-specific addition is that the people the note concerns are frequently alive, which raises what it must specify.
entries.application: Write the note early, as a working document, and let it discipline the drafting. If the note is getting longer and more defensive as the book progresses, the prose is making claims the research cannot support.

entries.name: Research That Has Become the Book's Purpose
entries.description: The failure state of a well-researched war novel is a book whose real subject is its own research.
entries.principle: Deep research produces an investment the writer will want returned, and the return comes as scenes that exist because the material exists. The symptom is a novel whose most confident passages are its explanations, and whose characters are most alive when demonstrating something.
entries.example: The technothriller makes this structural rather than accidental, because the accurate operation of systems is the pleasure the form promises — which is why it is the tradition where the failure is hardest to see and easiest to study.
entries.application: Identify the scenes that exist because you know something. Some of them are the book; the rest are the research asking to be paid, and cutting them is the last research task rather than a betrayal of it.

entries.name: The Soldier Who Is Not a Type
entries.description: The genre supplies a full set of ready-made soldiers, and each one arrives with an argument already inside it.
entries.principle: The hard NCO, the green lieutenant, the cynical veteran, the frightened replacement and the cross-section platoon are not neutral starting points. Each carries a claim about what military life does to people, and using one unexamined imports the claim along with the character.
entries.example: The cross-section ensemble is the clearest case: assembling one man of each background converts a unit into a demographic argument, and the argument is made whether or not the writer intended to make one.
entries.application: Take each character's type and give them one fact that the type forbids. If the character survives the contradiction, they are a person; if the contradiction has to be removed for the scene to work, the type is doing the writing.

entries.name: Rank Is Characterisation
entries.description: Position in a hierarchy determines what a character can know, say, refuse and be blamed for, and it does more characterising work than temperament.
entries.principle: Rank sets the information horizon, the vocabulary, the permissible register toward every other character, and the specific form of powerlessness available. Two people of different rank in the same room are having structurally different conversations, and writing them as equals with different jobs removes the pressure.
