entries.description: The American war novel written by a non-combatant, built partly from a cousin's letters and an army doctor's diary, awarded the Pulitzer and…
entries.text: The American war novel written by a non-combatant, built partly from a cousin's letters and an army doctor's diary, awarded the Pulitzer and criticised for both ever since. Its method is the prairie novel's patient attention to an ordinary interior life, applied to a young man who finds in the war the significance his life at home withheld — which is precisely the reading its critics found intolerable and the reason it remains the canon's sharpest test of the standing question.

entries.name: The Naked and the Dead
entries.author: Norman Mailer
entries.awards: None among the major American literary prizes (verified negative).
entries.description: The cross-section platoon at full ambition, published by a twenty-five-year-old who had served with a Pacific reconnaissance unit. Its Time Machine…
entries.text: The cross-section platoon at full ambition, published by a twenty-five-year-old who had served with a Pacific reconnaissance unit. Its Time Machine sections stop the war to deliver each man's civilian life entire, which is where the demographic argument enters the American war novel and where the form's characteristic cheat originates. The novel is simultaneously the template and the clearest study of the template's cost.

entries.name: From Here to Eternity
entries.author: James Jones
entries.awards: National Book Award for Fiction, 1952.
entries.description: The peacetime army as an institution with its own cruelty, in which the war arrives only at the end and functions as the answer to a question the…
entries.text: The peacetime army as an institution with its own cruelty, in which the war arrives only at the end and functions as the answer to a question the barracks has been asking for four hundred pages. Its subject is what a professional army does to the men inside it before any enemy appears, which makes it the canon's best account of the institution rather than the fighting.

entries.name: The Thin Red Line
entries.author: James Jones
entries.awards: None among the major American literary prizes (verified negative).
entries.description: A single company taking a single hill on Guadalcanal, with attention distributed across a dozen men and no protagonist rescued from the arithmetic.…
entries.text: A single company taking a single hill on Guadalcanal, with attention distributed across a dozen men and no protagonist rescued from the arithmetic. Jones was wounded on the island, and the novel's achievement is that the deaths land as accounting rather than as tragedy — the reader is never told which of these men matters, because the war did not distinguish either.

entries.name: Catch-22
entries.author: Joseph Heller
entries.awards: None among the major American literary prizes; its National Book Award status is carried as an unresolved item rather than asserted either way.
entries.description: The bureaucratic loop as the war's real logic, from a bombardier who flew sixty missions and took thirteen years to find the form. Its comic…
entries.text: The bureaucratic loop as the war's real logic, from a bombardier who flew sixty missions and took thirteen years to find the form. Its comic register breaks exactly once, deliberately and late, and the novel's entire structure is built around that break — which makes it the technical model for how a satiric war novel spends its tonal contract rather than merely maintaining it.

entries.name: Slaughterhouse-Five
entries.author: Kurt Vonnegut
entries.awards: None among the major American literary prizes (verified negative).
entries.description: The unwritable book written as its own failure to be written: the author opens by describing his inability to write it, and then declines to narrate…
entries.text: The unwritable book written as its own failure to be written: the author opens by describing his inability to write it, and then declines to narrate the firebombing of Dresden he survived as a prisoner of war. The unstuck chronology is a formal answer to a representation problem rather than a stylistic choice, and the repeated formula after each death accretes into an argument about numbness no single instance could make.

entries.name: The Caine Mutiny
entries.author: Herman Wouk
entries.awards: Pulitzer Prize for Fiction, 1952.
entries.description: The novel invites the reader to condemn a commander, allows them to, and then produces the case for the institution — leaving neither position…
entries.text: The novel invites the reader to condemn a commander, allows them to, and then produces the case for the institution — leaving neither position finally endorsed. It is the canon's most useful study of relief of command as an institutional act rather than a personal drama, and of the difference between a captain who is failing and a captain who is merely disliked by competent subordinates.

entries.name: Sword of Honour
entries.author: Evelyn Waugh
entries.awards: None among the major British literary prizes (verified negative; the trilogy predates the Booker Prize, first awarded 1969).
entries.description: Three novels published between 1952 and 1961, tracking a man who enlists for a crusade and discovers across six years that it does not exist. The…
entries.text: Three novels published between 1952 and 1961, tracking a man who enlists for a crusade and discovers across six years that it does not exist. The comedy is social and the argument is tragic: the absurdity is rendered as farce while the moral loss accumulates underneath it unremarked, and the book's real subject is the death of an idea of honour rather than any campaign.

entries.name: The Cruel Sea
entries.author: Nicholas Monsarrat
entries.awards: None among the major British literary prizes (verified negative).
entries.description: Atlantic convoy escort work written by an officer who did it, in which competent men are killed by circumstances their competence has no purchase…
entries.text: Atlantic convoy escort work written by an officer who did it, in which competent men are killed by circumstances their competence has no purchase on, repeatedly and without emphasis. Command exhaustion is rendered as an accumulating condition rather than as a crisis, and the sea is the stated antagonist — which lets the book treat the enemy as one hazard among several.

entries.name: Bomber
entries.author: Len Deighton
entries.awards: None among the major British literary prizes (verified negative).
entries.description: A single raid on a June night in 1943, narrated from the aircraft and from the German town beneath them, with the two halves given equal structural…
entries.text: A single raid on a June night in 1943, narrated from the aircraft and from the German town beneath them, with the two halves given equal structural weight. The moral equivalence is made by the book's architecture rather than asserted in its prose, which is why it remains the canon's best answer to the interiority-budget problem: the enemy is not given a speech, he is given a section of the novel.

entries.name: Die Stalinorgel
entries.author: Gert Ledig
entries.awards: No award record established; recorded as a documentation gap. The novel was driven out of print in West Germany and recovered only in the 1990s.
entries.description: Perhaps the most physically unbearable combat novel in the canon: seventy hours outside Leningrad, narrated by rotating among men who each see only…
entries.text: Perhaps the most physically unbearable combat novel in the canon: seventy hours outside Leningrad, narrated by rotating among men who each see only their own metre of the line and are killed mid-scene. It refuses the reader any vantage from which the action would cohere, which is the legibility problem answered at maximum severity — and its commercial failure at publication is itself evidence about what readers will accept.

entries.name: Das Boot
entries.author: Lothar-Günther Buchheim
entries.awards: No award record established; recorded as a documentation gap rather than a verified negative.
entries.description: The sealed-crew novel's definitive text, written by a war correspondent who made the patrol and spent thirty years on the book. Sound is the only…
entries.text: The sealed-crew novel's definitive text, written by a war correspondent who made the patrol and spent thirty years on the book. Sound is the only channel and the enemy exists as an instrument reading; the enclosure means the novel cannot glorify by spectacle because there is nothing to see. Its crew's total expertise is shown to be irrelevant to their fate, which is the argument.

entries.name: Wo warst du, Adam?
entries.author: Heinrich Böll
entries.awards: None for this title among the major prizes (verified negative); its author received the Nobel in Literature in 1972 for his work as a whole.
entries.description: The German retreat rendered as a sequence of loosely linked episodes in which the war is already lost and continues anyway. Böll served six years…
entries.text: The German retreat rendered as a sequence of loosely linked episodes in which the war is already lost and continues anyway. Böll served six years and was wounded four times, and the novel's method is the compressed encounter — a room, a road, a field hospital — carrying the condition of an entire army without describing it.

entries.name: Il sergente nella neve
entries.author: Mario Rigoni Stern
entries.awards: No award record established for the first edition; recorded as a documentation gap.
entries.description: The Italian retreat from Russia written by a sergeant of the Alpini who made it out, and the canon's clearest account of a withdrawal as a…
entries.text: The Italian retreat from Russia written by a sergeant of the Alpini who made it out, and the canon's clearest account of a withdrawal as a logistical and physical problem rather than a dramatic one. Its register is deliberately unliterary and its unit of attention is the next village, the next meal and the next night, which is what a retreat actually consists of.

entries.name: Il partigiano Johnny
entries.author: Beppe Fenoglio
entries.awards: None (published posthumously; verified negative).
entries.description: The partisan war without the Resistance myth, by a partisan who wrote it and never published it — the text appeared five years after his death.…
entries.text: The partisan war without the Resistance myth, by a partisan who wrote it and never published it — the text appeared five years after his death. Partisan warfare is rendered as cold, hungry and largely inconclusive, and the prose is deliberately strained through English syntax, which estranges the national material it describes and refuses the reader the patriotic register the subject invites.

entries.name: Прокляты и убиты
entries.author: Viktor Astafyev
entries.awards: No award record established for the novel itself; recorded as a documentation gap. Its author had earlier received major Soviet state prizes for other work.
entries.description: The late, furious repudiation of the Soviet war myth by a soldier who spent decades inside it, published in two volumes as the Soviet Union…
entries.text: The late, furious repudiation of the Soviet war myth by a soldier who spent decades inside it, published in two volumes as the Soviet Union collapsed. Its subject is the war's treatment of its own conscripts — the training camps, the starvation, the arbitrary executions — and it abandons the register of literary retrospection for something closer to accusation.

entries.name: В окопах Сталинграда
entries.author: Viktor Nekrasov
entries.awards: Stalin Prize, for 1946 (conferred 1947).
entries.description: The first honest Soviet Stalingrad novel, written by a combat engineer wounded there, and improbably decorated by the state whose war narrative it…
entries.text: The first honest Soviet Stalingrad novel, written by a combat engineer wounded there, and improbably decorated by the state whose war narrative it declined to supply. Its method is the restricted junior-officer horizon — the battle known only as far as the next position, with the strategic account entirely absent — which established the trench-level register that Soviet war fiction was not supposed to have.

entries.name: Сотнікаў
entries.author: Vasil Bykaŭ
entries.awards: No award record established for the novella in its original Belarusian publication; recorded as a documentation gap.
entries.description: Two captured partisans make opposite choices and the book refuses to award either. Its structural achievement is the reprisal arithmetic: every…
entries.text: Two captured partisans make opposite choices and the book refuses to award either. Its structural achievement is the reprisal arithmetic: every partisan action is paid for by civilians who were not consulted, and the novella stages that bill rather than eliding it — which makes it the canonical solution to a problem most resistance fiction avoids by construction.

entries.name: Nobi
entries.author: Ōoka Shōhei
entries.awards: Yomiuri Prize, 1951.
entries.description: A sick soldier is cut loose from any army in the Philippines and follows hunger to where it goes. The novel's first-person reliability degrades with…
entries.text: A sick soldier is cut loose from any army in the Philippines and follows hunger to where it goes. The novel's first-person reliability degrades with the narrator's body, so the reader cannot finally establish what was done — a formal solution to material that direct narration could not carry. Its antagonists are starvation and disease; the enemy army barely appears.

entries.name: The General
entries.author: C. S. Forester
entries.awards: None among the major British literary prizes (verified negative).
entries.description: Command psychology rendered without irony: a limited man executing his duty inside his own limitations, presented for the reader to judge rather…
entries.text: Command psychology rendered without irony: a limited man executing his duty inside his own limitations, presented for the reader to judge rather than judged by the narration. Written by an author medically rejected for service in the war he describes, it remains the sharpest study in the canon of how an officer of ordinary capacity issues an order that kills thousands and can account for every step of his reasoning.

entries.name: Once an Eagle
entries.author: Anton Myrer
entries.awards: No award record established; recorded as a documentation gap rather than a verified negative.
entries.description: Two officers followed across fifty years and two wars, so that institutional virtue and institutional ambition can be compared at every rank. Long…
entries.text: Two officers followed across fifty years and two wars, so that institutional virtue and institutional ambition can be compared at every rank. Long after its literary reputation faded it remained on professional military reading lists, which makes it an unusual object: a novel whose primary readership is the institution it depicts, and whose influence is therefore doctrinal as well as literary.

entries.name: Master and Commander
entries.author: Patrick O'Brian
entries.awards: None among the major British literary prizes (verified negative).
entries.description: The first of twenty novels in which technical competence is the literary pleasure on offer, with seamanship rendered so precisely that it functions…
entries.text: The first of twenty novels in which technical competence is the literary pleasure on offer, with seamanship rendered so precisely that it functions as characterisation. Its method is the unglossed technical vocabulary: the reader is trusted to sail on partial understanding, so expertise reads as lived competence rather than instruction — and the pleasure of that competence is exactly the mechanism the pack's craft collection asks writers to interrogate.

entries.name: HMS Ulysses
entries.author: Alistair MacLean
entries.awards: No award record established; recorded as a documentation gap.
entries.description: An Arctic convoy escort written by a man who served on them, and an attrition novel disguised as an adventure: the cast is killed systematically in…
entries.text: An Arctic convoy escort written by a man who served on them, and an attrition novel disguised as an adventure: the cast is killed systematically in conditions the author had endured, and the book supplies none of the relief its author's later work is built on. It is the clearest case in the commercial tradition of a writer using the adventure form against itself, once, before abandoning the attempt.

entries.name: The Hunt for Red October
entries.author: Tom Clancy
entries.awards: No literary award record established; recorded as a documentation gap.
entries.description: The technothriller's founding commercial text, published by a naval institute press. Its premise is a capability whose existence changes what…
entries.text: The technothriller's founding commercial text, published by a naval institute press. Its premise is a capability whose existence changes what everyone else must do, which is the accurate shape of a technological second-order effect — and its method is the competence sequence, a system explained while it is used, with the reader placed at the console and never under the ordnance. The pack cards it as the form's clearest specimen and its clearest structural problem.

entries.name: The Third World War: August 1985
entries.author: John Hackett
entries.awards: No literary award record established; recorded as a documentation gap.
entries.description: A future war written as history from beyond itself, by a general who had commanded at Arnhem and later the British Army of the Rhine, with a group…
entries.text: A future war written as history from beyond itself, by a general who had commanded at Arnhem and later the British Army of the Rhine, with a group of serving and retired officers. Its overtaking by events is the reason to card it: read now, it is a precise document of what a competent Western staff believed in 1978, and the pack treats the dated prediction as evidence rather than as a joke.

entries.name: The Killer Angels
entries.author: Michael Shaara
entries.awards: Pulitzer Prize for Fiction, 1975.
entries.description: Gettysburg delivered through the interiority of its real commanders on both sides, each held inside his own information horizon. Its dual-command…
entries.text: Gettysburg delivered through the interiority of its real commanders on both sides, each held inside his own information horizon. Its dual-command structure accepts the composite view as the price of its subject, and it reshaped the American battle novel toward command-level empathy. Note that its author, often described as a Korean War veteran, served as a sergeant in the 82nd Airborne before that war and saw no combat.

entries.name: The Heat of the Day
entries.author: Elizabeth Bowen
entries.awards: None among the major British literary prizes (verified negative).
entries.description: Wartime London rendered as a condition of consciousness rather than as a setting, by a novelist who served as an air-raid warden through the Blitz.…
entries.text: Wartime London rendered as a condition of consciousness rather than as a setting, by a novelist who served as an air-raid warden through the Blitz. Nothing is reliably knowable — about the war, about the man the protagonist loves, about who is telling the truth — and the plot turns on exactly that unreliability. It is the canon's strongest demonstration that the home front's material is atmosphere and information rather than event.

entries.name: Caught
entries.author: Henry Green
entries.awards: None among the major British literary prizes (verified negative).
entries.description: The Auxiliary Fire Service in the interval before the raids arrive, written during the war by a novelist serving in it. Its subject is waiting,…
entries.text: The Auxiliary Fire Service in the interval before the raids arrive, written during the war by a novelist serving in it. Its subject is waiting, social friction and administration rather than emergency, and its deliberately roughened prose — elided articles, broken idiom — lets speech and thought arrive without literary smoothing. The fire comes late and is almost an anticlimax, which is the point.

entries.name: The Balkan Trilogy
entries.author: Olivia Manning
entries.awards: None among the major British literary prizes (verified negative; the sequence predates the Booker Prize).
entries.description: Three novels published between 1960 and 1965 following two civilians retreating ahead of a war through Romania and Greece, with the marriage as the…
entries.text: Three novels published between 1960 and 1965 following two civilians retreating ahead of a war through Romania and Greece, with the marriage as the unit of narration. The war is experienced entirely through what it does to one relationship's daily negotiation — money, lodgings, whether to leave — which makes it the canon's most sustained account of displacement as a domestic condition.

entries.name: The World My Wilderness
entries.author: Rose Macaulay
entries.awards: None among the major British literary prizes (verified negative).
entries.description: Bombed London rendered as a wilderness that children colonise, by a writer who lost her flat and her library to the Blitz. The ruins are a place…
entries.text: Bombed London rendered as a wilderness that children colonise, by a writer who lost her flat and her library to the Blitz. The ruins are a place with their own social order rather than the absence of one, and the novel's disquiet comes from how quickly the new order becomes habitable — freedom and damage rendered as the same fact.

entries.name: The Slaves of Solitude
entries.author: Patrick Hamilton
entries.awards: None among the major British literary prizes (verified negative).
entries.description: War as accumulated small humiliation in a wartime boarding house outside London, with no front anywhere in sight. The war is present only as…
entries.text: War as accumulated small humiliation in a wartime boarding house outside London, with no front anywhere in sight. The war is present only as rationing, blackout and the impossibility of privacy, and the antagonist is a fellow lodger. It is the clearest case in the canon of a war novel generating its pressure entirely from constraint and proximity.

entries.name: At Mrs Lippincote's
entries.author: Elizabeth Taylor
entries.awards: None among the major British literary prizes (verified negative).
entries.description: The officer's wife in requisitioned lodgings, with the war supplying the pressure and never the subject. Its precisely observed social surface holds…
entries.text: The officer's wife in requisitioned lodgings, with the war supplying the pressure and never the subject. Its precisely observed social surface holds an unstated dissatisfaction, and the marriage is conducted under conditions neither party chose — which is the domestic register applied to a war happening entirely elsewhere, and a corrective to the assumption that the home front means the Blitz.

entries.name: The Night Watch
entries.author: Sarah Waters
entries.awards: Booker Prize shortlist, 2006 (verified as a shortlisting, not a win).
entries.description: Blitz London told backwards, from 1947 to 1941, so that every relationship is met at its end and then explained. The reverse chronology converts the…
entries.text: Blitz London told backwards, from 1947 to 1941, so that every relationship is met at its end and then explained. The reverse chronology converts the war from something the characters are moving through into something that has already determined them, and the ambulance-crew material renders the raids as a night shift with tasks rather than as spectacle.

entries.name: You Know When the Men Are Gone
entries.author: Siobhan Fallon
entries.awards: No major award record established; recorded as a documentation gap rather than a verified negative.
entries.description: Linked stories set almost entirely in the married quarters at Fort Hood during two Iraq deployments, written by a woman who lived there through…
entries.text: Linked stories set almost entirely in the married quarters at Fort Hood during two Iraq deployments, written by a woman who lived there through them. The base is rendered as a closed society with its own hierarchy, surveillance and etiquette, given the specificity usually reserved for the unit — which makes it the best single answer this canon offers to the pack's home-front problem. Carded as a story collection under the schema's convention.

entries.name: Le Silence de la mer
entries.author: Vercors
entries.awards: None (published clandestinely under occupation; verified negative).
entries.description: A cultivated German officer is billeted on a French household, and the household's refusal to speak to him is the entire action. Resistance is…
entries.text: A cultivated German officer is billeted on a French household, and the household's refusal to speak to him is the entire action. Resistance is rendered as an absence, which makes the occupier's monologues the only sound in the book and forces the reader to weigh a man who is personally decent and structurally intolerable. Published in secret by a press its author co-founded for the purpose.

entries.name: Suite française
entries.author: Irène Némirovsky
entries.awards: Prix Renaudot, 2004, awarded posthumously — an exception to the prize's normal rules.
entries.description: Written in 1941–42 by a novelist arrested and deported to Auschwitz before she could finish it, and published from the manuscript sixty years later.…
entries.text: Written in 1941–42 by a novelist arrested and deported to Auschwitz before she could finish it, and published from the manuscript sixty years later. Its achievement is the rendering of occupier and occupied at the same narrative depth, with class, property and manners persisting intact through catastrophe and observed without editorial. The exodus sequence is the canon's best account of a road full of civilians.

entries.name: 四世同堂
entries.author: Lao She
entries.awards: No award record established; recorded as a documentation gap.
entries.description: Eight years of Japanese occupation traced through one Beijing courtyard and four generations of one family, published in parts between 1944 and…
entries.text: Eight years of Japanese occupation traced through one Beijing courtyard and four generations of one family, published in parts between 1944 and 1948. Collaboration, resistance and mere survival are distributed across relatives, so every position is held by someone the reader knows — which is the structural solution to the moral-gradient problem that occupation fiction usually fails by supplying heroes and traitors.

entries.name: Wartime Lies
entries.author: Louis Begley
entries.awards: PEN/Hemingway Award, 1992.
entries.description: Survival in occupied Poland as continuous concealment, in which every social encounter is a hazard and every accommodation is defensible at the…
entries.text: Survival in occupied Poland as continuous concealment, in which every social encounter is a hazard and every accommodation is defensible at the moment it is made. The novel's cruelty is that survival requires becoming skilled at deception, and that the skill does not switch off afterwards — which is the aftermath problem arriving inside the occupation rather than after it.

entries.name: 色，戒
entries.author: Eileen Chang
entries.awards: No award record established; recorded as a documentation gap.
entries.description: A student resistance cell's plot against a collaborationist official, written by a novelist who spent the occupation in Shanghai. Its subject is the…
entries.text: A student resistance cell's plot against a collaborationist official, written by a novelist who spent the occupation in Shanghai. Its subject is the impossibility of maintaining a role, and its coldness is the point: the political and the erotic are rendered as the same transaction, with the novella refusing to supply the patriotic frame the material invites. Carded as a novella under the schema's convention.

entries.name: The Garden of Evening Mists
entries.author: Tan Twan Eng
entries.awards: Man Asian Literary Prize, 2012; Walter Scott Prize for Historical Fiction, 2013; Booker Prize shortlist, 2012.
entries.description: A Malayan survivor of Japanese internment apprentices herself to a Japanese gardener, with the reckoning arriving decades after the accommodation.…
entries.text: A Malayan survivor of Japanese internment apprentices herself to a Japanese gardener, with the reckoning arriving decades after the accommodation. The novel treats occupation as a sequence of survivable decisions whose meaning is only settled long afterwards, and it resolves into a subsequent emergency rather than into peace — refusing the ending the material appears to offer.

entries.name: Naples '44
entries.author: Norman Lewis
entries.awards: No major award record established; recorded as a documentation gap.
entries.description: An intelligence officer's diary of liberated Naples, in which liberation is administration, hunger, prostitution and black-market negotiation rather…
entries.text: An intelligence officer's diary of liberated Naples, in which liberation is administration, hunger, prostitution and black-market negotiation rather than deliverance. It is the canon's clearest account of what an occupying army actually does day to day, and of the specific squalor of being on the winning side of a city's collapse.

entries.name: Das siebte Kreuz
entries.author: Anna Seghers
entries.awards: No award record established for the original publication; recorded as a documentation gap. Written and published in exile while the camps it describes were operating.
entries.description: A fugitive escapes a concentration camp and passes through dozens of ordinary German lives, each of which must decide about him. The novel's…
entries.text: A fugitive escapes a concentration camp and passes through dozens of ordinary German lives, each of which must decide about him. The novel's structure is a distributed moral test administered to a whole population, which makes it the most useful resistance novel in the canon: the subject is not the escape but the ordinary people the escape interrogates.

entries.name: Ostře sledované vlaky
entries.author: Bohumil Hrabal
entries.awards: No award record established for the novella itself; recorded as a documentation gap.
entries.description: A sabotage operation carried out by a young man preoccupied with something else entirely, in which comic digression turns lethal without changing…
entries.text: A sabotage operation carried out by a young man preoccupied with something else entirely, in which comic digression turns lethal without changing register. The heroic act arrives inside a story that was not about heroism, which is the most honest available structure for resistance written by someone who lived through the occupation without performing one.

entries.name: Il sentiero dei nidi di ragno
entries.author: Italo Calvino
entries.awards: Premio Riccione, 1947.
entries.description: The partisan war seen by a child who understands none of its politics, written by a partisan at twenty-three. The band is rendered without…
entries.text: The partisan war seen by a child who understands none of its politics, written by a partisan at twenty-three. The band is rendered without idealisation — misfits, opportunists and the genuinely committed, indistinguishable to the narrator — and the reader must assemble the politics from behaviour alone, which is the child's-vantage device used without the sentimentality it usually buys.

entries.name: A Grain of Wheat
entries.author: Ngũgĩ wa Thiong'o
entries.awards: None (predates the major African and Commonwealth literary prizes; verified negative by date).
entries.description: The Mau Mau emergency and the betrayals inside the independence story, distributed across a community so that complicity cannot be assigned to a…
entries.text: The Mau Mau emergency and the betrayals inside the independence story, distributed across a community so that complicity cannot be assigned to a villain. Written on the eve of the author's turn away from English, it treats the resistance's own internal reckoning as the subject rather than the struggle against the colonial power, which is the harder book and the rarer one.

entries.name: The Moon Is Down
entries.author: John Steinbeck
entries.awards: None among the major American literary prizes for this title (verified negative); its author received the Nobel in Literature in 1962 for his work as a whole.
entries.description: Carded as the canon's clearest deliberate teaching failure. Written as morale work for occupied Europe and distributed clandestinely there to real…
entries.text: Carded as the canon's clearest deliberate teaching failure. Written as morale work for occupied Europe and distributed clandestinely there to real effect, it resolves the reprisal arithmetic in favour of resistance by construction: the occupiers are decent men in an impossible position and the occupied are steadfast. The craft is skilful and the purpose is avowed, which is precisely why it is the best available study of how a competent writer closes the gap on purpose.

entries.name: Der Vorleser
entries.author: Bernhard Schlink
entries.awards: Hans Fallada Prize, 1998; Prix Laure Bataillon, 1997, for the French translation — an award that indexes the translation rather than the original.
entries.description: The second-generation guilt novel, internationally successful and seriously contested. Its legal frame is the point — a narrator trained to weigh…
entries.text: The second-generation guilt novel, internationally successful and seriously contested. Its legal frame is the point — a narrator trained to weigh evidence applying that training to a person he cannot judge and cannot stop judging — and the dispute over whether its central device functions as mitigation is a live critical argument the pack records without settling.

entries.name: Draußen vor der Tür
entries.author: Wolfgang Borchert
entries.awards: None (verified negative; the author died the day after the first broadcast).
entries.description: A soldier returns and cannot get anyone to admit he has come back. The founding text of German Trümmerliteratur, written by a dying veteran of…
entries.text: A soldier returns and cannot get anyone to admit he has come back. The founding text of German Trümmerliteratur, written by a dying veteran of twenty-six, it compresses an entire return into a single night in expressionist form — and its central fact is not trauma but the absence of any structure willing to receive him. Carded as dramatic text under the schema's convention.

entries.name: Haus ohne Hüter
entries.author: Heinrich Böll
entries.awards: None for this title among the major prizes (verified negative); its author received the Nobel in Literature in 1972.
entries.description: Two fatherless households in the post-war Federal Republic, seen substantially through the children. The war is entirely in the past and entirely…
entries.text: Two fatherless households in the post-war Federal Republic, seen substantially through the children. The war is entirely in the past and entirely determinative, and the novel's subject is the social machinery — money, respectability, the sanctified dead father — by which a society converts its war into a story it can live with.

entries.name: 나목
entries.author: Park Wan-suh
entries.awards: Yeosong Donga Prize, 1970.
entries.description: A young woman working in a portrait shop for American soldiers in a Seoul that has changed hands four times, by a novelist who lost her brother in…
entries.text: A young woman working in a portrait shop for American soldiers in a Seoul that has changed hands four times, by a novelist who lost her brother in the war and began publishing at forty. Its subject is the specific exhaustion of a city that has been liberated and occupied repeatedly, and the flatness of surviving something that has not resolved.

entries.name: La tregua
entries.author: Primo Levi
entries.awards: Premio Campiello, 1963.
entries.description: The nine-month journey home from Auschwitz through a collapsing Europe, and the canon's most valuable account of the interval between survival and…
entries.text: The nine-month journey home from Auschwitz through a collapsing Europe, and the canon's most valuable account of the interval between survival and return. Liberation is rendered as the beginning of an administrative ordeal rather than as an ending, and the book's comic register — genuinely comic, in places — is what makes it the hardest of Levi's books to hold alongside the first.

entries.name: Se questo è un uomo
entries.author: Primo Levi
entries.awards: None for the first edition (verified negative; it was rejected by major publishers and issued in a small print run that largely went unsold).
entries.description: The definitive account of the camps, written immediately after the author's return by a chemist who survived Auschwitz. Its method is analytic…
entries.text: The definitive account of the camps, written immediately after the author's return by a chemist who survived Auschwitz. Its method is analytic restraint — a scientist's exactness that lets the material speak without rhetoric — and its refusal to raise its voice is the ethical form rather than a stylistic preference. The publication history is part of the record: the book found its readership only on reissue a decade later.

entries.name: I sommersi e i salvati
entries.author: Primo Levi
entries.awards: No major award record established; recorded as a documentation gap.
entries.description: The late essays that revise the survivor's authority downward, and the origin of the grey zone — the concept that made complicity discussable…
entries.text: The late essays that revise the survivor's authority downward, and the origin of the grey zone — the concept that made complicity discussable without collapsing the distinction between victim and perpetrator. Its central and most uncomfortable claim is that the ones best placed to testify are precisely the ones who did not survive, which is the pack's organising claim stated from inside the material.

entries.name: Sorstalanság
entries.author: Imre Kertész
entries.awards: None for the original publication (verified negative; the novel was initially rejected and attracted little attention). Its author received the Nobel in Literature in 2002.
entries.description: The formal achievement is the withheld hindsight: a fourteen-year-old narrator reports his own deportation as a sequence of reasonable-seeming…
entries.text: The formal achievement is the withheld hindsight: a fourteen-year-old narrator reports his own deportation as a sequence of reasonable-seeming steps, and is never granted knowledge he did not have at the time. The reader is denied the consolation of a survivor's wisdom, and the return home is the novel's most disquieting passage precisely because nothing is restored and the narrator declines to perform gratitude.

entries.name: Pożegnanie z Marią
entries.author: Tadeusz Borowski
entries.awards: No award record established; recorded as a documentation gap.
entries.description: The camps narrated by a functionary of the machinery who is neither innocent nor apologetic, in the flattest voice in the literature. The implicated…
entries.text: The camps narrated by a functionary of the machinery who is neither innocent nor apologetic, in the flattest voice in the literature. The implicated narrator describes his own participation in the same tone as everything else, refusing the reader any clean position from which to read — which is why it remains the hardest text in this category and the one that most directly refuses the rescuer's vantage. Carded as a story collection under the schema's convention.

entries.name: Les Bienveillantes
entries.author: Jonathan Littell
entries.awards: Prix Goncourt, 2006; Grand Prix du roman de l'Académie française, 2006.
entries.description: A former SS officer narrates the extermination in administrative detail across nine hundred pages, and the novel is contested on exactly that…
entries.text: A former SS officer narrates the extermination in administrative detail across nine hundred pages, and the novel is contested on exactly that ground: whether granting a perpetrator full interiority illuminates the mechanism or supplies him a voice he should not have. The pack records the dispute and adjudicates nothing. Its most defensible achievement is the bureaucratic rendering — mass killing as a logistics problem with meetings.

entries.name: Murambi, le livre des ossements
entries.author: Boubacar Boris Diop
entries.awards: No major award record established; recorded as a documentation gap.
entries.description: Written after a residency that brought African writers to Rwanda to look, and structured so that no single account can stand as the event: narration…
entries.text: Written after a residency that brought African writers to Rwanda to look, and structured so that no single account can stand as the event: narration is distributed across perpetrators, victims and returnees, with the perpetrator chapters given the same formal weight as the rest. It is built around a return to a site whose physical evidence is unavoidable and whose account remains contested.

entries.name: Notre-Dame du Nil
entries.author: Scholastique Mukasonga
entries.awards: Prix Renaudot, 2012; Prix Ahmadou Kourouma, 2012.
entries.description: A girls' boarding school in the years before the genocide, written by a woman who lost twenty-seven members of her family in it. The machinery of…
entries.text: A girls' boarding school in the years before the genocide, written by a woman who lost twenty-seven members of her family in it. The machinery of the later catastrophe is shown assembling inside an institution that believes itself ordinary — quotas, resentments, a teacher's casual taxonomy — which makes it the canon's clearest account of preparation rather than event.

entries.name: The Painted Bird
entries.author: Jerzy Kosiński
entries.awards: Prix du Meilleur Livre Étranger, 1966, for the French translation — an award indexing the translation. Carded as contested: from 1982 journalists disputed both the book's autobiographical status and the extent of the author's authorship, claims he and his defenders rejected. The pack states the dispute and adjudicates nothing.
entries.description: An episodic sequence of atrocities witnessed by a child in wartime Poland, delivered in a detached register whose power is inseparable from the…
entries.text: An episodic sequence of atrocities witnessed by a child in wartime Poland, delivered in a detached register whose power is inseparable from the truth-claim the disputes concern. It is carded because that inseparability is the lesson: a book whose effect depends on being taken as testimony is a different object once the testimony is contested, whatever the merits of the individual claims.

entries.name: Zdążyć przed Panem Bogiem
entries.author: Hanna Krall
entries.awards: No major award record established for the original publication; recorded as a documentation gap.
entries.description: The Warsaw Ghetto Uprising rendered as an interview with Marek Edelman, its last surviving commander, by a reporter who was herself a child survivor…
entries.text: The Warsaw Ghetto Uprising rendered as an interview with Marek Edelman, its last surviving commander, by a reporter who was herself a child survivor in hiding. The subject's evasions, corrections and refusals are left in place, so the reader watches testimony being produced rather than receiving it finished — which makes it the canon's best demonstration of the interview as a literary form.

entries.name: Записки блокадного человека
entries.author: Lidiya Ginzburg
entries.awards: No award record established; recorded as a documentation gap.
entries.description: The siege of Leningrad written as analysis rather than lament, in the third person, by a literary scholar who survived it and published four decades…
entries.text: The siege of Leningrad written as analysis rather than lament, in the third person, by a literary scholar who survived it and published four decades later. Hunger and cold are examined as changes in behaviour and cognition in a register borrowed from criticism, and the refusal of the first person is what gives the book its authority — the opposite of the strategy the material seems to demand.

entries.name: Жизнь и судьба
entries.author: Vasily Grossman
entries.awards: No award record established; recorded as a documentation gap. Completed in 1959, the manuscript was seized by the KGB in 1961 and the novel was published in Switzerland in 1980, sixteen years after the author's death.
entries.description: Stalingrad's military and civilian pressures held in one structure, with the two totalitarian systems rendered in parallel scenes at the same depth…
entries.text: Stalingrad's military and civilian pressures held in one structure, with the two totalitarian systems rendered in parallel scenes at the same depth — which is what made the book unpublishable in the Soviet Union. Its besieged house is a self-governing world with its own command, and its bureaucratic scenes show information being processed correctly into the wrong conclusion.

entries.name: Black Butterflies
entries.author: Priscilla Morris
entries.awards: Women's Prize for Fiction shortlist, 2023 (verified as a shortlisting, not a win).
entries.description: The siege of Sarajevo kept at the scale of one flat and one life, in which a painter watches the library burn and the city's social order…
entries.text: The siege of Sarajevo kept at the scale of one flat and one life, in which a painter watches the library burn and the city's social order renegotiate itself around scarcity. Its discipline is the refusal to escalate: the floor of deprivation is set early and not lowered for effect, which is the structural answer to the atrocity-ledger problem the siege form invites.

entries.name: The Cellist of Sarajevo
entries.author: Steven Galloway
entries.awards: No major award record established; recorded as a documentation gap.
entries.description: Three civilians and a counter-sniper in a besieged city, built around a real cellist's daily performance in the street. The counter-sniper sections…
entries.text: Three civilians and a counter-sniper in a besieged city, built around a real cellist's daily performance in the street. The counter-sniper sections give the waiting and withhold the satisfaction of the shot, and the novel's value to this pack is its treatment of a besieged routine as something people construct and maintain at cost, rather than as passive endurance.

entries.name: Kështjella
entries.author: Ismail Kadare
entries.awards: No award record established for the original Albanian publication; recorded as a documentation gap. Its author received the inaugural International Booker Prize in 2005, an author prize for a body of work rather than for a single title.
entries.description: A siege narrated from the besieging side's chronicler, which inverts the form's usual sympathy and makes the reader occupy the position of the army…
entries.text: A siege narrated from the besieging side's chronicler, which inverts the form's usual sympathy and makes the reader occupy the position of the army doing the starving. The bureaucracy of a siege — the engineers, the astrologer, the official account being drafted in real time — is the subject, and the fortress's interior is almost entirely withheld.

entries.name: Vergeltung
entries.author: Gert Ledig
entries.awards: No award record established; recorded as a documentation gap. Like its predecessor it was driven out of print and recovered only in the 1990s.
entries.description: Seventy minutes of an air raid on a German city, narrated by rotating among the people underneath it and the crews above, with biographical…
entries.text: Seventy minutes of an air raid on a German city, narrated by rotating among the people underneath it and the crews above, with biographical interpolations for characters who are already dead. It is the book the argument about German literature's failure to write the air war was conducted around, and its rejection by contemporary readers is part of what that argument is about.

entries.name: Der Untergang
entries.author: Hans Erich Nossack
entries.awards: No award record established; recorded as a documentation gap.
entries.description: Hamburg after the firestorm, written within months by a man who watched the raid from outside the city and returned to find it gone. Its register is…
entries.text: Hamburg after the firestorm, written within months by a man who watched the raid from outside the city and returned to find it gone. Its register is neither reportage nor lament but something closer to bewildered anthropology, and it is the earliest German attempt to find a form for the destruction of a city from inside the population that was destroyed.

entries.name: Kuroi ame
entries.author: Ibuse Masuji
entries.awards: Noma Literary Prize, 1966.
entries.description: Hiroshima in the register of a village chronicle, built from survivors' diaries and documents and serialised from January 1965. Radiation sickness…
entries.text: Hiroshima in the register of a village chronicle, built from survivors' diaries and documents and serialised from January 1965. Radiation sickness is rendered as a social condition affecting marriage prospects and daily life rather than as a medical event, and the novel repeatedly defers to quoted documentary text at its worst moments — the fiction stepping aside for the record.

entries.name: Natsu no hana
entries.author: Hara Tamiki
entries.awards: No award record established; recorded as a documentation gap. Publication was delayed by Occupation censorship.
entries.description: One of the earliest literary accounts of the atomic bombing, written within months by a survivor who was in Hiroshima on the day and who died by…
entries.text: One of the earliest literary accounts of the atomic bombing, written within months by a survivor who was in Hiroshima on the day and who died by suicide six years later. Its method is the present-tense inventory — what is seen, in order, without the retrospective frame that would organise it into an account — which is the least mediated writing in this category.

entries.name: Hotaru no haka
entries.author: Nosaka Akiyuki
entries.awards: Naoki Prize, for the second half of 1967 (announced January 1968).
entries.description: Two children starve after the firebombing of Kobe, in a story that announces both deaths at the outset so the narrative can proceed without suspense…
entries.text: Two children starve after the firebombing of Kobe, in a story that announces both deaths at the outset so the narrative can proceed without suspense and without the possibility of rescue. Written by a man whose younger sister died of malnutrition, it holds the child's-vantage device to an outcome it cannot console — which is what makes the use defensible where the same device usually purchases sentiment.

entries.name: Empire of the Sun
entries.author: J. G. Ballard
entries.awards: Guardian Fiction Prize, 1984; James Tait Black Memorial Prize, 1984; Booker Prize shortlist, 1984.
entries.description: A boy separated from his parents in Shanghai and interned, misreading the war continuously while the novel never softens what is being misread. Its…
entries.text: A boy separated from his parents in Shanghai and interned, misreading the war continuously while the novel never softens what is being misread. Its achievement is that the child's incomprehension produces no consolation: he survives by understanding the camp's economy better than the adults, and the liberation arrives as a further derangement rather than a rescue.

entries.name: Die Blechtrommel
entries.author: Günter Grass
entries.awards: Group 47 Prize, 1958, awarded for the excerpt read that year; the novel followed in 1959. Its author received the Nobel in Literature in 1999.
entries.description: A narrator who refuses to grow, narrating Danzig from the asylum, in which the grotesque is the only register that will hold the national material.…
entries.text: A narrator who refuses to grow, narrating Danzig from the asylum, in which the grotesque is the only register that will hold the national material. The formal decision — a witness whose deformity makes the material narratable at all — is the German post-war novel's most influential single solution, and its author's own late disclosure of Waffen-SS service is part of the book's reception history.

entries.name: The Boy in the Striped Pyjamas
entries.author: John Boyne
entries.awards: Irish Book Awards, 2006 and 2007; Bisto Book of the Year, 2007.
entries.description: Carded as a teaching failure. The child's incomprehension is sustained far past what the situation permits, and the ending redistributes the…
entries.text: Carded as a teaching failure. The child's incomprehension is sustained far past what the situation permits, and the ending redistributes the material's meaning toward the perpetrator's family — a structural choice that historians and Holocaust educators have criticised at length. It is included because it is enormously read, because its errors are precisely the ones the pack's craft collection screens for, and because the objections to it are a matter of public record rather than of taste.

entries.name: Rijāl fī al-shams
entries.author: Ghassan Kanafani
entries.awards: No award record established; recorded as a documentation gap.
entries.description: The founding text of Palestinian displacement fiction: three men attempt to cross a desert border inside a water tanker, and the novella ends…
entries.text: The founding text of Palestinian displacement fiction: three men attempt to cross a desert border inside a water tanker, and the novella ends without the arrival the journey has been driving toward. Its final question is left standing rather than answered, which is the formal refusal of the resolution the condition does not supply.

entries.name: باب الشمس
entries.author: Elias Khoury
entries.awards: Prix du Roman Arabe, 2008, for the French translation — an award indexing the translation.
entries.description: A nurse tells stories to an unconscious man in a Beirut hospital, accumulating decades of Palestinian testimony none of which can be confirmed.…
entries.text: A nurse tells stories to an unconscious man in a Beirut hospital, accumulating decades of Palestinian testimony none of which can be confirmed. Contradiction between versions is left standing as the book's argument rather than resolved, which makes it the canon's most sustained treatment of testimony that cannot be verified and must be told anyway.

entries.name: The Refugees
entries.author: Viet Thanh Nguyen
entries.awards: No major award record established for this title; recorded as a documentation gap. Its author received the Pulitzer Prize for Fiction in 2016 for a different book.
entries.description: Linked stories about people for whom the war ended decades ago and has not concluded, written across twenty years. Displacement is rendered after it…
entries.text: Linked stories about people for whom the war ended decades ago and has not concluded, written across twenty years. Displacement is rendered after it has become permanent and unremarkable to everyone except the displaced, and the collection declines to supply an ending for any of them. Carded as a story collection under the schema's convention.

entries.name: The Big Parade
entries.author: King Vidor
entries.awards: None (predates the Academy Awards, first presented 1929; verified negative by date). Added to the United States National Film Registry in 1992.
entries.description: The silent era's major American war film, and a primary screen text rather than an adaptation. Its middle section — an advance through woods under…
entries.text: The silent era's major American war film, and a primary screen text rather than an adaptation. Its middle section — an advance through woods under unseen machine-gun fire, staged at a metronomic pace — is the earliest sustained attempt to render combat as a mechanical process rather than as heroic action, and its returning-amputee ending refused the consolation the form was expected to supply.

entries.name: All Quiet on the Western Front (1930 film)
entries.author: Lewis Milestone
entries.awards: Academy Awards for Outstanding Production and Best Director, 1930. Note the credit convention of the period: the production award went to Carl Laemmle Sr., though Carl Laemmle Jr. produced. Added to the National Film Registry in 1990.
entries.description: The first major sound adaptation of the war novel, and the film that established the visual grammar of trench cinema — the tracking shot along a…
entries.text: The first major sound adaptation of the war novel, and the film that established the visual grammar of trench cinema — the tracking shot along a parapet, the boot passed from one dead conscript to the next. It was banned in Germany after organised disruption of its screenings, which makes its reception history part of the same record as the novel's.

entries.name: La Grande Illusion
entries.author: Jean Renoir
entries.awards: Academy Award nomination for Outstanding Production, 1938 — the first foreign-language film so nominated — and no win. Venice Film Festival, Best Artistic Ensemble, 1937.
entries.description: A prisoner-of-war film in which the escape structure is used to examine class and nationhood rather than to supply adventure, and in which the…
entries.text: A prisoner-of-war film in which the escape structure is used to examine class and nationhood rather than to supply adventure, and in which the escape resolves nothing about the war. Its central relationship crosses the lines and its central argument — that class loyalty may outlast national loyalty — was sufficiently unwelcome that the occupying authorities sought out and seized prints.

entries.name: Paths of Glory
entries.author: Stanley Kubrick
entries.awards: None — the film received no Academy Award nominations at all (verified negative, and a genuine one on the genre's most-cited anti-command film). Added to the National Film Registry in 1992.
entries.description: An impossible attack and the subsequent prosecution of its survivors staged as one continuous institutional process, with the camera refusing to…
entries.text: An impossible attack and the subsequent prosecution of its survivors staged as one continuous institutional process, with the camera refusing to make the assault exciting. It is the canon's cleanest study of the order that cannot be obeyed, and of exemplary punishment as an instrument aimed at spectators — and the refusal is total: no one is vindicated and the institution is undamaged.

entries.name: The Cranes Are Flying
entries.author: Mikhail Kalatozov
entries.awards: Palme d'Or, Cannes Film Festival, 1958.
entries.description: The Soviet war rendered almost entirely from the position of a woman who stays behind, in which the front appears briefly and the film's subject is…
entries.text: The Soviet war rendered almost entirely from the position of a woman who stays behind, in which the front appears briefly and the film's subject is waiting, rumour, requisitioned rooms and the absence of information. Its formal invention is a mobile camera used to convey subjective distress, and it recovered a civilian and specifically female vantage that Soviet war cinema had largely foreclosed.

entries.name: The Battle of Algiers
entries.author: Gillo Pontecorvo
entries.awards: Golden Lion, Venice Film Festival, 1966. Three Academy Award nominations across two non-consecutive ceremonies and zero wins — the film is routinely and wrongly described as Oscar-winning.
entries.description: Both organisations are given command structures, deliberations and interiority, so neither side is available to the audience purely as a threat. It…
entries.text: Both organisations are given command structures, deliberations and interiority, so neither side is available to the audience purely as a threat. It shows coercive interrogation functioning as an effective operational instrument and lets that stand as the disturbing finding rather than softening it, and it runs the reprisal exchange in both directions without pricing either for the viewer.

entries.name: The Green Berets
entries.author: John Wayne and Ray Kellogg
entries.awards: No major award record established; recorded as a documentation gap.
entries.description: Carded as a glorification teaching case, and the clearest documented instance of the military–entertainment arrangement in the canon: the production…
entries.text: Carded as a glorification teaching case, and the clearest documented instance of the military–entertainment arrangement in the canon: the production received extensive Department of Defense cooperation, and the record includes required script changes as a condition of that access. Its craft is competent and its purpose is avowed, which makes it more instructive than an incompetent film would be.

entries.name: Hearts and Minds
entries.author: Peter Davis
entries.awards: Academy Award for Best Documentary Feature, 1975.
entries.description: A documentary that cuts American official statement directly against Vietnamese testimony and lets the juxtaposition do the argument. Its…
entries.text: A documentary that cuts American official statement directly against Vietnamese testimony and lets the juxtaposition do the argument. Its most-discussed sequence places a general's remark about Asian attitudes to life beside a Vietnamese funeral, a montage that has been defended as devastating and attacked as manipulative since release — a dispute the pack records rather than settles.

entries.name: The Ascent
entries.author: Larisa Shepitko
entries.awards: Golden Bear, Berlin International Film Festival, 1977. Submitted as the Soviet entry to the 50th Academy Awards and not accepted as a nominee — a submission, not a nomination.
entries.description: Two Soviet partisans are captured and make opposite choices, in the most severe treatment of the reprisal and collaboration problem on film. The…
entries.text: Two Soviet partisans are captured and make opposite choices, in the most severe treatment of the reprisal and collaboration problem on film. The interrogator is a former teacher who reasons rather than threatens, and the film declines to award either prisoner's decision — which is Bykaŭ's structure rendered without the consolation of authorial sympathy.

entries.name: The Deer Hunter
entries.author: Michael Cimino
entries.awards: Five Academy Awards including Best Picture and Best Director, 1979. The sole "Screenplay by" credit is Deric Washburn, with Cimino holding story credit only following Writers Guild arbitration, which he contested. Added to the National Film Registry in 1996.
entries.description: A working-town community before, during and after the war, in which the aftermath sections carry more of the film than the combat does. Its…
entries.text: A working-town community before, during and after the war, in which the aftermath sections carry more of the film than the combat does. Its Russian-roulette sequences have been contested since release as having no documented basis, which is a live dispute the pack records; and its aftermath is rendered almost entirely as fear and damage, with what the characters did there left largely outside the account.

entries.name: Apocalypse Now
entries.author: Francis Ford Coppola
entries.awards: Palme d'Or, Cannes Film Festival, 1979, shared with The Tin Drum. Two Academy Awards, for Cinematography and Sound, 1980. Added to the National Film Registry in 2000.
entries.description: The war as a river journey into a private kingdom, and the canon's most influential demonstration that a war film's spectacle can be simultaneously…
entries.text: The war as a river journey into a private kingdom, and the canon's most influential demonstration that a war film's spectacle can be simultaneously its subject and its problem. Its helicopter assault is the most imitated sequence in the genre and the most exact illustration of the pack's entertainment problem: the scene is an indictment and a thrill in the same frames, and audiences have taken it both ways for four decades.

entries.name: Das Boot (1981 film)
entries.author: Wolfgang Petersen
entries.awards: Six Academy Award nominations and zero wins, 1983 — the film is frequently misdescribed as an Oscar winner.
entries.description: The novel's enclosure rendered as sound design: no horizon, no visual field, the enemy present only as a bearing and a sonar return, and the hull's…
entries.text: The novel's enclosure rendered as sound design: no horizon, no visual field, the enemy present only as a bearing and a sonar return, and the hull's integrity as the entire plot. It is the screen's best demonstration that a war film can generate sustained tension without spectacle, and that a form which cannot glorify by display has to find another way to be exciting — which is where its own risk lies.

entries.name: Gallipoli
entries.author: Peter Weir
entries.awards: No verified award record established in this build; recorded as a documentation gap rather than a verified negative.
entries.description: Two Australian sprinters enlist and one of them is killed in a diversionary attack at the Nek. The film's final image is powerful and is constructed…
entries.text: Two Australian sprinters enlist and one of them is killed in a diversionary attack at the Nek. The film's final image is powerful and is constructed to deliver a single emotional stroke, which simplifies the mechanism that produced the deaths — a legitimate choice that the pack cards precisely because the simplification is so effective and so widely mistaken for the history.

entries.name: Come and See
entries.author: Elem Klimov
entries.awards: Golden Prize, Moscow International Film Festival, 1985. Submitted as the Soviet entry to the 58th Academy Awards and not accepted as a nominee — a submission, not a nomination. No National Film Registry listing exists or can exist for a Soviet production.
entries.description: The German anti-partisan campaign in Belarus seen through a boy who cannot process what he is shown, built from the burned-villages testimony that…
entries.text: The German anti-partisan campaign in Belarus seen through a boy who cannot process what he is shown, built from the burned-villages testimony that the Belarusian documentary tradition assembled. It refuses both explanation and spectacle and has no consoling movement anywhere in it. Carded at the highest tier because it is the canon's strongest evidence that atrocity can be represented without being made consumable.

entries.name: Platoon
entries.author: Oliver Stone
entries.awards: Four Academy Awards including Best Picture and Best Director, 1987. Added to the National Film Registry in 2019.
entries.description: The infantry war as a moral contest between two sergeants, written and directed by a veteran of the campaign it depicts. Its village sequence is the…
entries.text: The infantry war as a moral contest between two sergeants, written and directed by a veteran of the campaign it depicts. Its village sequence is the canon's most-seen depiction of an atrocity committed by the viewpoint side, and its contacts run well past the interval doctrine and experience describe — the film needs the duration, and the need is visible.

entries.name: Grave of the Fireflies (1988 film)
entries.author: Isao Takahata
entries.awards: None in the Academy record (verified negative). The animation medium and the film's distribution history kept it outside the awards apparatus that its stature would otherwise imply.
entries.description: The animated adaptation of the Kobe firebombing story, which announces both children's deaths in its opening moments and proceeds without suspense…
entries.text: The animated adaptation of the Kobe firebombing story, which announces both children's deaths in its opening moments and proceeds without suspense or the possibility of rescue. It is the strongest available refutation of the assumption that animation softens material, and the clearest case of the child's-vantage device held to an outcome it cannot console.

entries.name: Three Kings
entries.author: David O. Russell
entries.awards: No major award record established; recorded as a documentation gap. Story credit is held by John Ridley following a documented dispute.
entries.description: Four American soldiers go looting after the 1991 ceasefire and collide with the uprising the coalition had encouraged and did not support. Its…
entries.text: Four American soldiers go looting after the 1991 ceasefire and collide with the uprising the coalition had encouraged and did not support. Its formal invention is the interior ballistic shot — the film stops to show what a round does to an organ — which converts the genre's habitual bloodlessness into a specific physiological claim, and its subject is the political consequence of a war declared over.

entries.category: Civil Wars and the Late Twentieth Century
entries.name: No Man's Land
entries.author: Danis Tanović
entries.awards: Academy Award for Best Foreign Language Film, 2002, and the Golden Globe in the same category — the only film in this pack's screen set to win both.
entries.description: A Bosnian and a Serb soldier trapped in the same trench with a third man lying on a mine, while United Nations peacekeepers and international…
entries.text: A Bosnian and a Serb soldier trapped in the same trench with a third man lying on a mine, while United Nations peacekeepers and international journalists arrive to manage the situation. Its subject is the machinery of intervention and observation rather than the combat, and its ending refuses every party the resolution the apparatus promises.

entries.name: Pearl Harbor
entries.author: Michael Bay
entries.awards: Academy Award for Sound Editing, 2002. Six Golden Raspberry nominations and zero wins — the film is often described as a Razzie winner and was not.
entries.description: Carded as a teaching case in both failure directions at once. The attack is rendered substantially from the point of view of the descending…
entries.text: Carded as a teaching case in both failure directions at once. The attack is rendered substantially from the point of view of the descending ordnance, which is the aesthetic the pack's craft collection exists to refuse; and the losses are converted into demonstrations of the surviving protagonists' worth. Its technical accomplishment is real, which is what makes it useful rather than merely bad.

entries.name: Waltz with Bashir
entries.author: Ari Folman
entries.awards: Golden Globe for Best Foreign Language Film, 2009. Academy Award nomination in the same category and no win — the film is routinely written up as Oscar-winning.
entries.description: An animated documentary in which a former Israeli soldier reconstructs his own suppressed memory of proximity to the Sabra and Shatila massacre by…
entries.text: An animated documentary in which a former Israeli soldier reconstructs his own suppressed memory of proximity to the Sabra and Shatila massacre by interviewing others who were there. Its subject is the unreliability of the witness rather than the event, and its final shift out of animation into archive footage is the formal decision the whole film is built to earn.

entries.name: The Hurt Locker
entries.author: Kathryn Bigelow
entries.awards: Six Academy Awards including Best Picture and Best Director, 2010. Three Golden Globe nominations and zero wins — the film swept the Oscars and BAFTA, not the Globes. Added to the National Film Registry in 2020.
entries.description: An explosive ordnance disposal team in Iraq, rendered as a sequence of discrete operations each of which produces an event. That rhythm is the…
entries.text: An explosive ordnance disposal team in Iraq, rendered as a sequence of discrete operations each of which produces an event. That rhythm is the opposite of the deployment it depicts, and the pack cards it for exactly that tension: it is the most decorated film of its war and its structure is an argument about addiction that the operational reality does not support.

entries.name: Restrepo
entries.author: Tim Hetherington and Sebastian Junger
entries.awards: Grand Jury Prize for Documentary, Sundance Film Festival, 2010. Academy Award nomination for Best Documentary Feature and no win. Its News and Documentary Emmy belongs to the editor and is a distinct body from the Primetime Emmys.
entries.description: A year with one platoon at an outpost in the Korengal valley, filmed by two correspondents who stayed. It records the empty patrol at its real…
entries.text: A year with one platoon at an outpost in the Korengal valley, filmed by two correspondents who stayed. It records the empty patrol at its real frequency, shows materially dominant operations altering nothing, and ends with the outpost's abandonment — which makes it the clearest available evidence for the pack's rule that technological asymmetry wins engagements and does not end wars.

entries.name: Act of Valor
entries.author: Mike McCoy and Scott Waugh
entries.awards: No major award record established; recorded as a documentation gap.
entries.description: Carded as the canon's most explicit institutional production: a feature film starring serving Navy special-warfare personnel, made with service…
entries.text: Carded as the canon's most explicit institutional production: a feature film starring serving Navy special-warfare personnel, made with service cooperation under which the Navy held final approval of the cut. It is the clearest single object in the pack for studying what an entertainment product looks like when the institution depicted controls the representation, and it is analysed here as craft rather than condemned as policy.

entries.name: Land of Mine
entries.author: Martin Zandvliet
entries.awards: Academy Award nomination for Best Foreign Language Film, 2017, and no win.
entries.description: German prisoners, most of them boys, are made to clear mines from the Danish coast after the surrender, under a sergeant who begins by hating them.…
entries.text: German prisoners, most of them boys, are made to clear mines from the Danish coast after the surrender, under a sergeant who begins by hating them. It reverses the custodian and prisoner positions the captivity form usually assumes, and its subject is what a victorious population does with its defeated in the interval when the law is least observed and least observed by anyone.

entries.name: Dunkirk
entries.author: Christopher Nolan
entries.awards: Three Academy Awards, for Film Editing, Sound Editing and Sound Mixing, 2018 — the film did not win Best Picture or Best Director. Three Golden Globe nominations and zero wins.
entries.description: An evacuation told on three timelines of different lengths running to the same point, with almost no dialogue and no enemy shown. Its scale is…
entries.text: An evacuation told on three timelines of different lengths running to the same point, with almost no dialogue and no enemy shown. Its scale is rendered structurally rather than numerically, which sidesteps the number-that-becomes-people problem rather than solving it, and its commemorative function is built into the form rather than examined by it.

entries.name: The Things They Carried
entries.author: Tim O'Brien
entries.awards: Pulitzer Prize for Fiction finalist, 1991 — a finalist and not a winner, a distinction publishers' copy routinely erases. Prix du Meilleur Livre Étranger, 1992, an award indexing the French translation.
entries.description: Linked stories that make the unauditability of testimony their subject: accounts are told, retracted and retold inside the same book, and the…
entries.text: Linked stories that make the unauditability of testimony their subject: accounts are told, retracted and retold inside the same book, and the narrator states directly that a true war story is not the same thing as a story that happened. It is the canon's most influential answer to the pack's fourth diagnostic question, and its opening inventory of carried objects is an index of what each man cannot say.

entries.name: Matterhorn
entries.author: Karl Marlantes
entries.awards: No major award record established; recorded as a documentation gap rather than a verified negative.
entries.description: A hill is fortified, abandoned and retaken at a cost the novel itemises, by a decorated Marine officer who worked on the book for roughly three…
entries.text: A hill is fortified, abandoned and retaken at a cost the novel itemises, by a decorated Marine officer who worked on the book for roughly three decades. Its achievement is procedural exactness carried to a moral end — the radio traffic, the resupply, the medical evacuation and the leech-infested water rendered in full — so that the arithmetic rather than the rhetoric is what indicts.

entries.name: Thân phận của tình yêu
entries.author: Bảo Ninh
entries.awards: Vietnam Writers' Association Award, 1991; Independent Foreign Fiction Prize, 1994, an award indexing the English translation.
entries.description: The war told from the winning side as unbearable loss, by a veteran of a North Vietnamese youth brigade, and officially disfavoured for years…
entries.text: The war told from the winning side as unbearable loss, by a veteran of a North Vietnamese youth brigade, and officially disfavoured for years afterwards. Its collapsed chronology is a veteran writing a novel he cannot order, with the disorder presented as the only honest sequence available. Note that the survival statistics widely attached to the author's unit originate in publishers' copy and are not independently sourced.

entries.name: The Sympathizer
entries.author: Viet Thanh Nguyen
entries.awards: Pulitzer Prize for Fiction, 2016; Andrew Carnegie Medal for Excellence in Fiction, 2016; Edgar Award for Best First Novel, 2016.
entries.description: A confession written under duress by a double agent for a reader who is also his interrogator, so every sentence is doing two jobs. Its sustained…
entries.text: A confession written under duress by a double agent for a reader who is also his interrogator, so every sentence is doing two jobs. Its sustained refusal of the American frame around a Vietnamese war is the point, and its treatment of a Hollywood production shooting the war is the canon's sharpest account of how a conflict is converted into someone else's entertainment.

entries.category: Civil Wars and the Late Twentieth Century
entries.name: Half of a Yellow Sun
entries.author: Chimamanda Ngozi Adichie
entries.awards: Orange Prize for Fiction, 2007; named Women's Prize for Fiction "Winner of Winners", 2020.
entries.description: The Biafran war carried through the collapse of intimate lives, written by a novelist born seven years after it ended and built from family…
