entries.text: The Biafran war carried through the collapse of intimate lives, written by a novelist born seven years after it ended and built from family testimony and research — which makes it the standing question's best modern test case. Its lucid realism is a deliberate stance rather than a default: clarity maintained against obscurity, so the horror registers through fully rendered character.

entries.name: Redeployment
entries.author: Phil Klay
entries.awards: National Book Award for Fiction, 2014; W. Y. Boyd Literary Award for Excellence in Military Fiction, 2015 — the American Library Association awards the year after the copyright year, which is why one book carries two prizes a year apart.
entries.description: Twelve narrators doing twelve different jobs in the same war — mortuary affairs, artillery, chaplaincy, public affairs, civil affairs — each story…
entries.text: Twelve narrators doing twelve different jobs in the same war — mortuary affairs, artillery, chaplaincy, public affairs, civil affairs — each story built from the vocabulary and moral frame of a specific occupation. The war is assembled from positions rather than described from one, and the author served as a Marine public affairs officer rather than as an infantryman. Carded as a story collection under the schema's convention.

entries.name: Sozaboy
entries.author: Ken Saro-Wiwa
entries.awards: No major award record established; recorded as a documentation gap.
entries.description: The Nigerian civil war narrated in an invented idiom the author subtitled rotten English — a deliberately unstable register built for a narrator…
entries.text: The Nigerian civil war narrated in an invented idiom the author subtitled rotten English — a deliberately unstable register built for a narrator with no language in which to describe what happens to him. The construction is the argument: the boy soldier's incomprehension is a property of the vocabulary available to him rather than of his intelligence. Its author was executed by the Nigerian state ten years after publication.

entries.name: Band of Brothers
entries.author: Tom Hanks and Erik Jendresen, developed for television
entries.awards: Primetime Emmy Award for Outstanding Miniseries, 2002; Golden Globe Award for Best Miniseries, 2002. Note the credit: Steven Spielberg and Tom Hanks are executive producers rather than creators, and the series was developed by Hanks and Jendresen.
entries.description: A single parachute infantry company followed from training to occupation, and the most influential sustained soldier's-eye account on television.…
entries.text: A single parachute infantry company followed from training to occupation, and the most influential sustained soldier's-eye account on television. Its warmth is also its difficulty, and the pack cards it partly for that: the unit-as-family structure means the losses are made to purchase the bond that makes them grievable, which is the glorification trap operating with complete sincerity.

entries.name: Generation Kill
entries.author: David Simon and Ed Burns, from Evan Wright
entries.awards: Two Primetime Creative Arts Emmy Awards, 2009; all three of its Primetime Emmy nominations lost. The Creative Arts and Primetime ceremonies are distinct bodies and are frequently merged in citation.
entries.description: A reconnaissance battalion's advance to Baghdad, adapted from an embedded reporter's account, with the profanity, boredom and radio traffic left at…
entries.text: A reconnaissance battalion's advance to Baghdad, adapted from an embedded reporter's account, with the profanity, boredom and radio traffic left at full strength. It renders the vehicle crews' private language without glossing it, and its refusal to supply an arc is the point — the invasion arrives, proceeds and stops, and nobody in it is changed in the way the form expects.

entries.name: Un village français
entries.author: Frédéric Krivine, Philippe Triboit and Emmanuel Daucé
entries.awards: No verified award record established in this build; recorded as a documentation gap.
entries.description: Seven seasons following one French town from the arrival of German troops in 1940 to the reckonings decades afterwards. Its achievement is the…
entries.text: Seven seasons following one French town from the arrival of German troops in 1940 to the reckonings decades afterwards. Its achievement is the accumulation of small accommodations: officials become complicit through the ordinary performance of their jobs, with no decisive moment of choice anywhere — which is the moral-gradient problem solved at a length no novel could sustain.

entries.name: Unsere Mütter, unsere Väter
entries.author: Stefan Kolditz and Philipp Kadelbach
entries.awards: International Emmy Award, 2014 — the International Emmys are a distinct body from the Primetime Emmys.
entries.description: Five young Germans followed from 1941 to the war's end, and a major popular attempt to place ordinary German complicity on prime-time television.…
entries.text: Five young Germans followed from 1941 to the war's end, and a major popular attempt to place ordinary German complicity on prime-time television. Its reception is part of the card: the series drew sustained criticism, particularly in Poland, over its depiction of the Home Army, and that dispute is recorded here rather than adjudicated.

entries.name: Blackadder Goes Forth
entries.author: Richard Curtis and Ben Elton
entries.awards: BAFTA recognition is on the record but the specific ceremony year could not be reconciled in this build; recorded as a documentation gap.
entries.description: A sitcom set in a First World War trench whose final minutes abandon comedy entirely for a silent advance. Its influence on popular understanding of…
entries.text: A sitcom set in a First World War trench whose final minutes abandon comedy entirely for a silent advance. Its influence on popular understanding of the war is larger than its intent: the preening incompetent staff officer is substantially this series' bequest, and it is the single most effective transmitter of the donkeys-and-lions reading that professional historians have spent decades qualifying.

entries.name: The World at War
entries.author: Jeremy Isaacs
entries.awards: No verified award record established in this build; recorded as a documentation gap.
entries.description: Twenty-six hours of documentary assembled while a very large number of participants at every level were still alive to be interviewed, from cabinet…
entries.text: Twenty-six hours of documentary assembled while a very large number of participants at every level were still alive to be interviewed, from cabinet ministers to camp survivors to Hitler's secretary. Its method is testimony gathered before the accounts had consolidated, which makes it a primary source about memory as well as a history — and its refusal of triumphal framing set the register for the form.

entries.name: M*A*S*H
entries.author: Larry Gelbart, developed for television
entries.awards: Multiple Primetime Emmy Awards across its run, including Outstanding Comedy Series, 1974. Note the credit: the series is "developed by" Larry Gelbart rather than created by him.
entries.description: A field hospital in Korea, made during Vietnam and understood at the time to be about the later war. Its medical material is the most sustained…
entries.text: A field hospital in Korea, made during Vietnam and understood at the time to be about the later war. Its medical material is the most sustained treatment of the casualty chain in popular television, and its rear-area setting made the war a place of administration and exhaustion rather than of combat — the longest-running argument in the medium that the war's centre is not the front.

entries.name: Hearts of Iron IV
entries.author: Paradox Development Studio
entries.awards: No academy award record established; recorded as a documentation gap rather than a verified negative.
entries.description: The pack's logistics card, and a system that makes the player run a war economy: civilian and military factories, dockyards, resources, division…
entries.text: The pack's logistics card, and a system that makes the player run a war economy: civilian and military factories, dockyards, resources, division templates, manpower and supply as interlocking constraints. It teaches the thing no novel can dramatise — that operational choice is largely determined by production allocation months earlier. Two facts belong on the record: it was banned in China in 2017 for non-compliance with local law, and its modding communities have been documented as attracting a minority of extremist participation, with moderation in place. Both are named and neither is adjudicated.

entries.name: Combat Mission
entries.author: Battlefront.com
entries.awards: No academy award record established; recorded as a documentation gap.
entries.description: Its simultaneous-turn system is the closest mechanical model of command anyone has built: both sides enter orders during a pause and are then…
entries.text: Its simultaneous-turn system is the closest mechanical model of command anyone has built: both sides enter orders during a pause and are then powerless for a sixty-second execution phase, able only to move the camera. That is the epistemic condition of command made into a rule — you commit, then you watch, and you cannot intervene — and no prose device reproduces it, because prose cannot take the pen away from the reader.

entries.name: Foxhole
entries.author: Siege Camp
entries.awards: No academy award record established; recorded as a documentation gap.
entries.description: Logistics performed by other human beings: every soldier consumes a supply item on spawning, and players gather raw resources, refine them,…
entries.text: Logistics performed by other human beings: every soldier consumes a supply item on spawning, and players gather raw resources, refine them, manufacture ammunition and fortifications and drive them to the front across a persistent map in wars lasting weeks. The rear echelon is played rather than described, which makes the game's actual subject the boredom and indispensability of the people prose leaves out.

entries.name: Spec Ops: The Line
entries.author: Yager Development
entries.awards: No wins at any of the four games academies; nominated at D.I.C.E. for Outstanding Achievement in Story and did not win. Its press awards — Inside Gaming, IGN — are press bodies rather than academies. The gap between a thin award record and an enormous influence is itself the card.
entries.description: The medium's central anti-war work, and the one that makes the player rather than the character the object of the critique. Its white-phosphorus…
entries.text: The medium's central anti-war work, and the one that makes the player rather than the character the object of the critique. Its white-phosphorus sequence has the player fire indirect munitions through a targeting display and then walk through the civilian dead, and its loading-screen text degrades from helpful to accusatory until it addresses the player directly about why they are still playing. The designers anticipated players blaming them for the choice, which is the argument: the player could have stopped.

entries.name: This War of Mine
entries.author: 11 bit studios
entries.awards: Independent Games Festival Audience Award, 2015; Games for Change Best Gameplay, 2015; International Mobile Gaming Award for Best Meaningful Play, 2016. Nominated at D.I.C.E. for Outstanding Achievement in Story, 2015, and did not win. The publisher's "over one hundred awards" figure includes press and event awards and is not an academy record.
entries.description: The civilian-perspective game: the player manages non-combatant survivors in a besieged city, balancing health, hunger and morale, and must decide…
entries.text: The civilian-perspective game: the player manages non-combatant survivors in a besieged city, balancing health, hunger and morale, and must decide whether to steal from an elderly couple to keep their own group alive. Failure is not defeat but documented despair. In 2020 the Polish government added it to a recommended reading list for high schools, reported as the first time a state placed a video game on a school list — the pack's best external evidence that games are constitutive of this genre rather than a courtesy inclusion.

entries.name: Papers, Please
entries.author: Lucas Pope
entries.awards: Seumas McNally Grand Prize, Excellence in Narrative and Excellence in Design, Independent Games Festival, 2014; Innovation Award and Best Downloadable Game, Game Developers Choice Awards, 2014; BAFTA Games Award for Best Simulation Game, 2014 — and it lost BAFTA Best Game, Game Design and Game Innovation in the same year. A Peabody Award in the interactive category is on the record with an unreconciled year designation, noted as such.
entries.description: Carded under the pack's condition-of-being-at-war lane rather than as combat or command: an immigration booth in a state at war, where the player is…
entries.text: Carded under the pack's condition-of-being-at-war lane rather than as combat or command: an immigration booth in a state at war, where the player is paid per processed document and their family starves if they are slow. Mercy is therefore priced, and complicity becomes a time-pressured input task — the most economical model of administrative complicity in any medium.

entries.name: Valiant Hearts: The Great War
entries.author: Ubisoft Montpellier
entries.awards: Annie Award for Outstanding Achievement, General Audience Animated Short, 2015. Nominated at The Game Awards 2014 for Best Narrative and at BAFTA Games 2015 for Artistic Achievement, and won neither.
entries.description: Puzzle-adventure form applied to the First World War, with soldiers' letters and archival material integrated as collectible rewards — which is…
entries.text: Puzzle-adventure form applied to the First World War, with soldiers' letters and archival material integrated as collectible rewards — which is simultaneously its achievement and the honest objection to it, since the historical record is delivered as a prize for solving something. Made in partnership with documentary producers, it is the clearest case of a game teaching a war's material while its own reward structure argues against the teaching.

entries.name: Six Days in Fallujah
entries.author: Highwire Games
entries.awards: None found; recorded as a documentation gap given its early-access status. Carded as a contested case: real battle, real dead on both sides, living veterans on both sides. The pack analyses the game and the documented dispute only, and says nothing about the battle itself.
entries.description: Announced in 2009, cancelled when its publisher withdrew, revived in 2021 and released into early access in 2023. Objections on the record came from…
entries.text: Announced in 2009, cancelled when its publisher withdrew, revived in 2021 and released into early access in 2023. Objections on the record came from coalition veterans, Iraqi civilians, anti-war organisations and bereaved military families, on grounds of recency, trivialisation and the exclusion of civilian context. The developers cite over seventy interviews with Marines, Iraqi civilians and others; their public position on whether the game is political changed between 2009 and 2021, and after release the studio acknowledged that loading-screen commentary carried only American perspectives and announced plans to add others.

entries.name: America's Army
entries.author: United States Army
entries.awards: Three Guinness World Records, 2009 — records rather than awards, and there is no academy award record. Online functionality was withdrawn in 2022.
entries.description: Carded at the lowest tier, and not as a close call. This is not a war game with a recruiting effect; it is a recruiting instrument that took the…
entries.text: Carded at the lowest tier, and not as a close call. This is not a war game with a recruiting effect; it is a recruiting instrument that took the form of a war game, conceived by the Army's chief economist and described on the record as a strategic communication device. It was costed against television advertising per person-hour. The craft failure is structural rather than incidental: the game cannot hold the gap open, because closing it was the commission.

entries.name: Call of Duty 4: Modern Warfare
entries.author: Infinity Ward
entries.awards: D.I.C.E. Overall Game of the Year, 2008. At BAFTA it won the publicly voted GAME Award, which is not BAFTA's Best Game — that went to BioShock for the same year. The four Game of the Year awards frequently disagree and must never be collapsed; this title is the canonical demonstration.
entries.description: The game that set the modern military shooter's template, and the pack's standing illustration of the awards problem in this medium. Its craft is…
entries.text: The game that set the modern military shooter's template, and the pack's standing illustration of the awards problem in this medium. Its craft is genuinely innovative — the aircraft-gunship level, in which the player kills at total remove through a monochrome sensor display, is the medium's most-cited treatment of the distance kill — and its commercial descendants are where the genre's glorification trap now operates at the largest scale.

entries.name: Maus
entries.author: Art Spiegelman
entries.awards: Pulitzer Prize Special Award in Letters, 1992 — a special citation rather than a win in an established Pulitzer category. Eisner Awards; National Book Critics Circle Award nomination.
entries.description: The transmission of a war across a generation, made the book's subject: a son extracting his father's Auschwitz account, failing to receive it, and…
entries.text: The transmission of a war across a generation, made the book's subject: a son extracting his father's Auschwitz account, failing to receive it, and rendering his own discomfort at making a work from it inside the work. Its animal conceit is a formal argument about racial categories rather than a device for softening, and its second volume's account of the author's success and guilt is the canon's most honest treatment of what it costs to card another person's catastrophe.
